title: Senior Software Engineer, AppSTAR COMPASS
descriptionHtml:
Be a founding engineer on a brand-new team building security review for the LLM age. You'll design and write the platform that evaluates every code change tens of thousands of engineers ship, and clears the vast majority without a human ever touching it.

Security review has always been a bottleneck. A developer ships a change, waits for someone to look at it, and the security team drowns in a queue it can never fully clear. We're ending that tradeoff. Our engine evaluates changes as they happen, decides how much scrutiny each one actually needs, and handles the common case automatically with no wait for the developer and no queue for the reviewer.

The team is funded and forming now, and the first engineers will set the architecture. That means real design ownership, not a codebase you inherit, and experienced security engineers backing you with the risk expertise so you build against what actually matters. If you want to work on agentic systems where the correctness bar is high and the impact is measurable, this is the seat.

Set the architecture for a greenfield platform, not maintain someone else's
Build agentic and automated evaluation running continuously at very high volume
Ship something measurable: fewer manual reviews, faster releases, no added burden on developers

Key job responsibilities
- Design and build the core of an event-driven platform that evaluates code changes for security risk, routes the small fraction needing human attention, and clears the rest automatically.
- Own significant technical decisions end to end: data flow, evaluation pipeline, service boundaries, storage, and the tradeoffs behind each one.
- Build and tune the automated evaluation layers, including agentic checks, and the mechanisms that keep their decisions accurate over time.
- Partner closely with the security team that defines how risk is evaluated, turning their criteria into production code that runs reliably at scale.
- Work directly with the security engineers who handle escalated changes, building the queues, context, and tooling that make their reviews fast.
- Build the developer-facing experience: clear, trustworthy visibility into what was evaluated, what happened, and why, with as close to zero required action as possible.
- Negotiate and implement the integrations with adjacent platform and telemetry teams the system depends on.
- Raise the engineering bar on a new team: code review, design review, testing strategy, operational readiness, and on-call fundamentals from the start.
- Mentor engineers and help interview and grow the team as it scales.

A day in the life
You'll spend most of your time designing and writing code on a system that doesn't exist yet: how an event moves through the pipeline, where automated checks fire, what happens when confidence drops. You'll pair with security engineers to pressure-test whether your evaluation logic catches what it should. Some days you're in a design review defending a boundary decision, or debugging why a class of change is getting routed wrong at volume. Early on you'll help shape the roadmap and interview the engineers who join next.

About the team
We decide how security attention gets spent. Our customers are the engineers shipping code every day and the security engineers reviewing it, and both are paying a tax we think is unnecessary. Our mission is to remove it: make security assurance automatic, proportional to real risk, and visible to the people it protects. We're small, new, and unusually close to the outcome. We care more about getting the decision right than about being the ones who make it, and we'd rather encode expertise into a mechanism than hoard it.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture
In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 5+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience
- 5+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: Sr. ICT Design Engineer, Data Center Design Engineering
descriptionHtml:
About AWS Infrastructure Services
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we're the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we're looking for talented people who want to help.

You'll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
________________________________________
About the Role
As a Senior ICT Design Engineer, you will serve as a technical leader within a global engineering organization comprised of highly effective Architects, Structural, Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, Security, and Controls Engineers. You will be a primary driver of ICT design strategy, standards, and quality across multiple data center builds, regions, and partner teams.

At AWS, we're revolutionizing the design of critical communications pathways, spaces, and cabling within our data centers. We're looking for a senior technical leader who can set the standard for ICT design excellence, drive cross-discipline coordination, and accelerate our time to market — while mentoring the next generation of ICT engineers and influencing the broader infrastructure architecture.

In this role, you will own complex, multi-site ICT design programs from concept through construction administration. You will lead design reviews, define engineering standards, engage with industry suppliers and standards bodies, and drive the adoption of emerging technologies. Your contributions will have deep and far-reaching impact on partner teams, regional infrastructure architecture, and the overall AWS global data center portfolio.

This role offers a rare opportunity to shape the future of ICT design at AWS at a systems and architecture level — where your decisions influence not just individual projects, but the long-term scalability, cost-efficiency, and resilience of AWS infrastructure worldwide.

Key job responsibilities
Technical Leadership & Design Ownership
• Lead the design, development, and delivery of scalable, high-performance fiber optic and copper plant designs, pathway systems, and ICT specifications across multiple simultaneous builds and regions.
• Own the ICT architecture for complex, large-scale data center programs — including new campus greenfield builds, build-to-suit (BTS) projects, and colocation environments — ensuring designs are extensible, cost-optimized, and aligned with AWS BOD standards.
• Drive the development and continuous improvement of ICT design standards, BOD templates, specification sections, and QA/QC checklists used across the global DE organization.
• Identify and resolve complex cross-discipline coordination challenges involving civil, architectural, electrical, mechanical, and security systems, removing bottlenecks that impact project delivery.
• Take a long-term view of infrastructure design decisions, balancing short-term project needs against global architectural consistency and future scalability.
Standards, Quality & Process Improvement
• Define and enforce ICT engineering best practices, design standards, and quality benchmarks across the team and partner organizations.
• Lead and conduct design milestone reviews (30%, 60%, 90%, 100%) for ICT systems, providing technical feedback that elevates design quality across the portfolio.
• Review and approve ICT pathway, cabling, and equipment submittals, ensuring compliance with AWS standards, applicable codes, and project-specific requirements.
• Drive root-cause analysis for endemic design deficiencies and lead programmatic initiatives to resolve them — leaving systems better, simpler, and easier to maintain.
• Contribute to and lead Correction of Errors (COE) processes and Lessons Learned reviews, translating findings into actionable BOD or standards improvements.
Cross-Discipline & Stakeholder Collaboration
• Serve as the primary ICT technical point of contact for complex projects and regional programs, engaging directly with Design Managers, TPMs, Construction Managers, Security Engineers, and partner discipline leads.
• Collaborate with the Security, Electrical, Civil, and Architectural disciplines to ensure ICT pathway and cabling designs are fully coordinated and constructible.
• Partner with SPEAR, DCESS, and other AWS security stakeholders to ensure ICT designs support physical security system integration requirements (access control, CCTV, PIDS, etc.).
• Engages cross-functionally with stakeholder teams including Networking, Hardware Engineering, Network Deployment, Operations, and Capacity Planning to gather technical requirements, align on constraints, and develop infrastructure designs that meet organizational objectives and operational standards.
• Engage with industry suppliers, manufacturers, and standards bodies (TIA, BICSI, IEEE) to define product requirements, evaluate emerging technologies, and influence AWS procurement strategy.
• Support the RFP process by developing ICT scope requirements, reviewing vendor bids, and providing technical input on consultant selection and scope comprehension.
Innovation & Emerging Technology
• Identify, evaluate, and champion new ICT technologies, construction methods, and design approaches that improve infrastructure quality, reduce cost, and accelerate installation timelines.
• Lead or contribute to programmatic initiatives that drive innovation across the ICT design portfolio (e.g., unified cabling platforms, modular pathway systems, next-generation fiber architectures).
• Stay current on data center technology trends and provide informed recommendations on which technologies are appropriate for AWS facilities and which are not.
Mentorship, Hiring & Talent Development
• Actively mentor and develop ICT engineers, improving their technical knowledge, design skills, and ability to deliver independently.
• Lead and participate in the hiring process, including conducting technical interviews and providing calibrated assessments for ICT engineering candidates.
• Provide technical assessments for DCIE promotion evaluations, contributing to the professional development of colleagues across the organization.
• Train and onboard new team members on ICT architecture, AWS design standards, and cross-discipline coordination processes.
Program Execution & Travel
• Identify and respond to design risks and high-priority issues rapidly and effectively, escalating through appropriate channels when required.
• Travel 25%+ to conduct site visits, lead in-person design reviews, coordinate with onsite personnel and contractors, and validate ICT infrastructure at AWS data centers globally.

About the team
*Why AWS*
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

*Diverse Experiences*
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

*Work/Life Balance*
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

*Inclusive Team Culture*
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

*Mentorship and Career Growth*
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related field
- 5+ years of experience in industrial or commercial engineering in mission-critical facilities, including but not limited to: data centers, power generation, or telecommunications infrastructure.
- 5+ years of ICT design experience in Mission Critical Environments, with demonstrated ownership of complex, multi-site design programs.
- 5+ years of experience developing and leading the production of design documentation (plans, specifications, BOD templates, QA/QC checklists) for construction and/or permitting.
- 5+ years of hands-on experience with fiber optic components, cabling, interconnect products, technologies, and applicable standards (TIA-568, TIA-569, TIA-942, BICSI TDMM/OSPDRM).
- Demonstrated experience driving engineering standards, design best practices, or process improvements across a team or organization.
- Experience leading cross-discipline design coordination in a large-scale infrastructure or construction program.
- BICSI RCDD Certification or internationally recognized equivalent (e.g., CDCDP, DCDC, CCTT, CNIDP).
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

Preferred qualifications

- Professional Engineering or Architectural License
- Experience developing or contributing to BOD-level design standards, master specifications, or engineering guidelines for a multi-site infrastructure portfolio.
- Experience with building codes, AHJ requirements, and permitting processes across multiple jurisdictions or regions.
- Demonstrated ability to carry design concepts from exploration and development through to deployment or mass production across multiple builds.
- Experience reading, interpreting, and producing construction drawings, specifications, and submittal documents at a senior level of ownership.
- Proficiency with AutoCAD, Revit, Bluebeam, and MS Office Suite.
- Experience engaging with industry standards bodies (TIA, BICSI, IEEE) or contributing to industry publications, patents, or technical standards.
- Familiarity with physical security system integration requirements (access control, CCTV, PIDS) as they relate to ICT pathway and cabling design.
- Experience supporting or leading RFP processes, vendor evaluations, and design consultant management.

title: Maintenance Manager
descriptionHtml:
Operations is at the heart of Amazon's business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. The Reliability & Maintenance Engineering (RME) team are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it happen. We drive continuous improvement and maintain all the robotics and material handling equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey!

About the Role:
As a Maintenance Manager, you will transform workplace environments by leading maintenance operations across your site and developing the next generation of maintenance leaders. In this critical role, you'll oversee Area Maintenance Managers and their teams, develop strategic maintenance programs, and drive operational excellence across multiple functional areas. You will blend strategic planning, financial management, and leadership development while navigating between managing preventative maintenance programs, coordinating with operations teams, and responding to emergencies that require quick, decisive action. You'll balance proactive planning with real-time problem resolution while fostering a culture of safety, innovation, and continuous improvement.

What Do We Offer?
Amazon offers competitive compensation packages including comprehensive healthcare benefits starting on Day 1, matching 401(k) program, and up to 20 weeks of paid parental leave. But wait, there's more: We provide lightweight fire-resistant daily wear and composite toe safety shoes for your safety!


Key job responsibilities
• You will provide leadership and mentorship to Area Maintenance Managers and their teams of service technicians and automation engineers, fostering professional growth and performance
• You will develop and maintain comprehensive preventative maintenance programs, manage department budgets, and drive continuous improvement initiatives across the site
• You will ensure rigorous adherence to safety protocols and procedures across all operational sites while partnering with site Safety leadership to implement and audit safety programs

• You will travel domestically up to 15% to support network-level initiatives and provide guidance across multiple sites

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, Engineering Technology, Reliability Engineering, or 2+ years of Amazon RME (BB/3P) Full Time Exempt experience
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
- 5+ years of industrial maintenance experience
- 4+ years of direct leadership/supervisory experience
- 4+ years of managing department spend and labor budgets, performing root cause analysis (RCA), and implementing continuous improvement (CI) experience
- 4+ years of managing, analyzing and communicating results to senior leadership experience
- 4+ years of Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) experience

Preferred qualifications

- Professional Engineer License
- Experience working with Material Handling Equipment (MHE) integrators
- Experience in project management
- Experience with statistical analysis
- Experience maintaining material handling equipment and integrated systems
- Master's degree, or Six Sigma Black Belt certification
- Experience leading network level/multi-site maintenance organizations

title: Operations Engineer, Global Engineering Services
descriptionHtml:
Amazon created one of the most sophisticated supply chains in the world. From the introduction of Amazon Prime, to the use of advanced technology for package delivery, Amazon consistently drives change from the front of the pack.

Amazon is searching for an innovative and solutions-oriented Operations Engineer to be a part of our global initiative of developing and delivering the next generation of world-class fulfillment systems. Successful candidates are natural self-starters who have prior engineering experience in the integrated automation project life cycle, including development, design, implementation, enhancement, and support.

As an Operations Engineer for Amazon Fulfillment, you will work with some of the most talented engineers in the design, development, and delivery of physical distribution systems around the globe. You are responsible for managing a technology or integration project, successfully delivering the solution to meet project goals. You may work directly with external equipment vendors, customers, or partners, and you have a solid understanding of the design approaches and industry technologies utilized in fulfillment and distribution center designs. To meet timelines and minimize disruption to support teams, you manage the overall schedule, proactively mitigate risks, and keep the scope of engineering deliverables under control.

You must be responsive, flexible, and able to succeed within an open collaborative environment. Amazon’s culture encourages innovation and expects engineers to take a high-level of ownership in solving complex problems.

Come help us make history!

Key job responsibilities
- Work independently with internal and external engineering teams to deliver high-quality, cross-functional projects on-time, on-budget, with low defects and maintainable outcomes.
- Partner with project managers and external vendors to set priorities, establish milestones, and drive schedules to meet deadlines.
- Influence and review technical documentation, diving deep into system layouts and solutions, and competently represent designs to customers and other teams.
- Communicate project status clearly and concisely to leadership, effectively answering questions in detail and producing regular summaries.
- Develop strong working relationships with vendors, engineers, managers, peers, FC/SC leadership, operations teams, and business stakeholders (Launch, Facilities, Finance, Safety, Process Engineers) across multiple sites.
- Participate in design reviews and support execution between internal teams and vendors, including equipment specifications, material flow, process design, and site layout.
- Manage budget documents, change order controls, purchase orders, and invoicing. Identify and lead process improvement initiatives in support of operations teams within a geographic node.
- Travel up to 50% domestically, with variable intensity including up to three weeks consecutively, including weekends.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of industrial engineer, operations engineer, manufacturing engineer, or project engineer in a manufacturing environment experience
- Bachelor's degree

Preferred qualifications

- Knowledge of AutoCAD, VBA, and SQL at the intermediate level
- Experience working with and managing third party vendors
- Experience with Six Sigma, lean manufacturing

- French, German, Polish, Arabic, Portuguese, Turkish, Chinese (Mandarin), Afrikaans and Zulu are considered preferred qualifications.

descriptionHtml:

title: Manager, Customs Brokerage, Amazon Customs & Trade
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Global Logistics (AGL) manages the international movement of goods into and across Europe, supporting Amazon's mission to be Earth's most customer-centric company. As part of a strategic programme to bring customs clearance capability in-house, we are building a dedicated Customs Brokerage function within Amazon Customs & Trade.

We are looking for a Manager, Customs Brokerage to own risk management and compliance operations across our Netherlands (NL) customs clearance network. This individual contributor role carries end-to-end accountability for the performance of customs brokerage operations in the Netherlands, covering ocean, air, rail and road shipments for both third-party and first-party entry filing.

You will be the primary point of contact with Dutch customs authorities, responding to regulatory queries, managing document inspections, and resolving compliance holds. You will develop risk management frameworks, establish operational controls, and drive compliance excellence across all customs activities. You will also lead the strategic direction for the Netherlands: identifying automation opportunities, onboarding new business lines, and acting as the subject matter expert who helps replicate what gets built here across other European markets.

This role blends operational execution with strategic leadership. Expect roughly 40% of your time on frontline customs operations (shipment clearance, compliance holds, documentation) and 60% on strategic work (regulatory change management, project prioritisation, automation design, and cross-functional advisory to senior leadership).

You will influence and mentor customs operators based in other locations through a dotted-line relationship, owning overall country performance without direct line management to start.

Key job responsibilities
**Risk Management & Compliance Leadership**

- Develop and implement risk management frameworks for customs brokerage activities across NL operations

- Serve as the licensed point of contact with Dutch customs authorities, managing regulatory queries, document inspections, and compliance escalations

- Monitor regulatory developments, assess business impact, and translate changes into actionable procedures and scalable solutions

- Lead holistic operational excellence programmes linking policies, SOPs, internal controls, monitoring, and reporting

**Strategic & Technology Leadership**

- Own the strategic roadmap for NL customs brokerage, identifying projects that deliver competitive advantage

- Drive automation of manual customs and logistics processes by influencing product and technology teams; design scalable, compliant solutions rather than relying on manual workarounds

- Onboard new business lines (e.g. AWS) into the NL customs operation

- Act as the subject matter expert supporting expansion of the in-house customs model to other European markets


**Operational Execution**

- Oversee daily customs clearance performance, proactively identifying systemic risks and exception trends

- Ensure documentation accuracy, tariff classification integrity, and clearance SLA adherence across all transport modes

- Lead cross-functional collaboration with sellers, vendors, third-party brokers, and internal operations teams

- Provide regular reporting and insights to senior leadership on risk posture and mitigation strategies


**Stakeholder Management**

- Work directly with Dutch customs authorities, building trusted relationships and influencing outcomes

- Partner with Finance, Legal, Accounting, Tax, and technology teams for comprehensive risk assessments

- Mentor and guide customs operators (based in Prague and China) through dotted-line influence, driving performance standards and knowledge sharing

A day in the life
Your day begins by reviewing overnight customs clearance activity and scanning dashboards for SLA performance and exception trends. You sync with the operations team to understand overnight issues: perhaps a shipment held for additional documentation, or a new regulatory interpretation that could affect clearance procedures. You assess whether these are isolated incidents or systemic risks requiring immediate action.

Mid-morning, you take a call from Dutch customs about a document inspection on a batch of shipments. You pull together the required documentation, liaise with the broker team in Prague to confirm the details, and respond within the deadline.

In the afternoon, you shift to strategic work. A recent regulatory change removed the low-value duty threshold and introduced a minimum handling charge per package. You have already implemented a manual workaround to keep shipments flowing. Now you are designing the automation that handles this at scale, working with the technology team to build it into the system permanently. You present the proposal to senior leadership with a clear cost-benefit analysis.

Later, you join a cross-functional call about onboarding a new business line into the Netherlands. You advise on the customs implications, document requirements, and risk profile, and agree the timeline for go-live.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- Experience engaging with regulatory agencies in permit applications or equivalent
- Experience building cross-functional partnerships and influencing stakeholders across the organization to act without having a direct reporting relationship
- Speak, write, and read fluently in Dutch
- Proven progressive experience in NL customs brokerage, compliance, audit, or risk management, with at experience in a leadership or strategic role

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree or equivalent
- Experience developing and implementing of standards, policies and programs or equivalent
- Experience leveraging technology and implementing lean principles / Six Sigma methodologies to drive process improvements or equivalent
- Knowledge of Microsoft Office products and applications at an advanced level
- Experience in warehouse operations and logistics or equivalent
- - Experience with Dutch customs declaration systems (AGS, DMS) or equivalent EU systems

In this role, you'll work with utilities, regulators, and local authorities to deliver high-voltage transmission and substation infrastructure on time, on budget, and to specification. You'll manage grid compliance across a growing portfolio of sites, structure and negotiate energy contracts, and develop strategies that keep pace with Australia's evolving regulatory landscape as the grid decarbonizes and decentralizes.
This role offers the opportunity to shape how AWS connects to the Australian grid at scale, balancing rapid infrastructure expansion with technical compliance and long-term energy strategy. If you're energized by the intersection of energy infrastructure and technology and want to work on problems that directly enable the next generation of cloud services, we'd like to hear from you.

This role is based in Melbourne. 10% travel may be required.

Key job responsibilities
• Serve as the single-threaded owner for grid connection delivery across AWS data centers in Melbourne, from initial due diligence through energization, directly enabling cloud capacity growth.
• Lead relationships with transmission network service providers (TNSPs), distribution network service providers (DNSPs), and regulators to secure grid capacity and negotiate connection agreements that meet AWS timelines.
• Coordinate across internal teams (Planning, Real Estate, Design, Procurement, Construction, Operations, Finance, and Commissioning) to align power infrastructure delivery with broader site schedules, resolving dependencies and removing blockers.
• Conduct power due diligence for new data center sites, assessing grid capacity, connection feasibility, redundancy requirements, and long-term supply reliability.
• Develop and negotiate utility contracts, energy services agreements (ESAs), and connection agreements, ensuring commercial terms align with AWS standards and regional market conditions.
• Own technical grid compliance across the portfolio, ensuring all connections meet National Electricity Rules (NER), grid codes, and relevant Australian standards.
• Interface with government bodies, market operators (AEMO), and regulatory authorities to obtain approvals, influence policy development, and ensure AWS infrastructure expansion objectives are supported.
• Manage capital budgets for power infrastructure delivery, tracking expenditure against forecasts and identifying cost optimization opportunities.
• Develop strategies to reduce energy costs and improve supply resilience, including assessment of emerging grid technologies, tariff structures, and alternative supply arrangements.

A day in the life
Your morning might start with a call to a network service provider, working through connection application timelines or resolving a technical query with the design engineering team for a new substation. By midday, you're reviewing grid compliance documentation with the design team, ensuring submissions to AEMO align with National Electricity Rules. In the afternoon, you could be negotiating commercial terms on an energy services agreement or presenting a capital expenditure forecast to finance stakeholders.
You'll manage multiple concurrent projects at different stages of delivery, from early-stage site due diligence through to energization. No two days look the same, but the thread that connects them is ensuring AWS has the grid capacity it needs, when it needs it, to support growth across Melbourne.

About the team
The APAC Energy & Water team is a multi-disciplinary group covering energy, water, energy procurement, carbon free energy, and strategic partnerships, all working to keep AWS data centers powered, cooled, and connected across the region. This role sits within the energy function, where you'll be part of a team that thrives on solving complex infrastructure problems, building strong utility relationships, and finding creative ways to bring power to some of the most ambitious projects in the country. We work hard, we back each other, and we genuinely enjoy what we do.

Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

- 6+ years of solving problems with technology in the Energy & Utilities industries experience
- Bachelor's degree, or 5+ years of directly managing and being responsible for multiple large projects experience
- Experience with budgeting, scheduling and cost/benefit analysis

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in data centers, infrastructure service providers, or related technology companies
- Experience in one of project management, planning, engineering, developing or constructing substations or other 66kV or greater energy infrastructure
- High level technical understanding of MV & HV Transmission Line and substation, with familiarity of local grid code, grid connectivity procedures, grid application procedures and roles and responsibilities, standards of performance of Distribution/Transmission Utilities

title: Sr Content Delivery Manager , Amazon MGM Studios
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Senior Content Delivery Manager based in Tokyo to lead content delivery and launch operations for Amazon MGM Studios growing Japan Originals slate. This role will serve as the strategic operational leader for Studio Content Services (SCS) in Japan, partnering closely with local Post Production and Production teams, the Global Delivery Manager, and teams across Studio Content Services, supporting both original productions and acquisitions for Amazon MGM Studios.

The Sr. Content Delivery Manager will lead the end-to-end Studio Content Services operational framework for Japan — designing and optimizing processes for intake, launch, and asset management while ensuring that each title (Movies and Series) receives successful: a) definition of deliverables, b) appropriate quality assurance for Original Version deliverables, c) timely intake of needed materials into Studio systems and processes, d) clean support for all streaming launch activities, and e) appropriate asset storage and management for downstream usage. The Sr. Content Delivery Manager will serve as the primary Studio Content Services point of contact for assigned titles, overseeing delivery schedules, solving complex challenges with internal stakeholders and external vendors, and ensuring content is delivered on time, on budget, and to the highest quality standards.

This role will lead the coordination of intake and launch operational support between the Japan-based operation and Amazon’s LA-based Global SCS teams, ensuring that local Japanese needs and time-zone requirements are addressed even while aspects of operations are handled elsewhere. The role requires building and implementing Studio Content Services operational strategies for the Japan territory — making trade-offs between short- and long-term needs, mitigating risk, and balancing speed, quality, and resource constraints as the Originals slate scales significantly.

This position is responsible for identifying and resolving complex operational challenges, making effective trade-offs between delivery timelines and studio release plans, and driving clear communication across languages, time zones, and organizational boundaries. The ideal candidate will be both tactical and strategic — comfortable managing multiple series and movies annually while simultaneously designing long-term solutions, scaling workflows, influencing partner teams to establish and grow Studio Content Services operations in Japan.

Key job responsibilities
1. Serve as the strategic Content Delivery leader for Japan, partnering with Japan Post Production, Global Delivery Manager, Studio Content Services Prime Video Delivery Operations and senior leaders to drive cross-functional initiatives and influence long-term operational goals, and author strategic documents (eg delivery SOPs, process improvements, slate status reports) to drive alignment.
2. Own and drive the on-time, on-budget delivery of movies and series produced and acquired in Japan, including partnering with Post on delivery budgets, ensuring all required assets are complete and delivered according to schedule.
3. Lead negotiations on delivery schedules with outside studios, producers, and production companies to meet overall release goals, make independent decisions on lower risk trade-offs and escalate high impact decisions as appropriate.
4. Actively manage intake processes for assigned titles, assess complex issues, mitigate risk, and drive resolution — serving as an escalation point for operational challenges across the Japan content pipeline.
5. Establish and maintain regular operational connection points between the Japan-based team and Global Studio Content Services in LA — including recurring status reporting, cross-timezone syncs, and intake/launch readiness checkpoints — to ensure continuous alignment and visibility across teams.
6. Drive best practices with external vendor relationships to deliver content on time and within budget, providing strategic guidance on technical requirements, QC processes, and operational expectations.
7. Identify, assess, and resolve technical or operational risks to delivery timelines that might impact studio release plans — proactively mitigating long-term risk rather than only escalating.
8. Design, implement, and continuously improve delivery guidelines and operational procedures, driving consistency and operational excellence across the Japan content pipeline and influencing standards globally.
9. Navigate organizational and process ambiguity in a fast-evolving environment, building operational strategies within a business-strategy context and adapting to shifting priorities, new workflows, and evolving team structures as the Japan Originals slate scales.
10. Advocate for and influence Japan-specific operational needs within the broader Global Studio Content Services framework, building strategic relationships with key stakeholders, and shaping processes and priorities to ensure effective local delivery.
11. Serve as the gatekeeper for sensitive communications between internal and external partners, exercising judgment on when to elevate information and when to limit communications to protect operational and business interests.


A day in the life
No two days look the same — and that’s by design. You’ll start your day syncing with the Global Studio Content Services team in LA before they sign off, and then shift focus to Japan-based partners across Post Production, production companies, and local vendors. A typical day includes managing active title pipelines, reviewing QC results, troubleshooting delivery blockers before launch windows, negotiating schedules with external studios, and driving intake / launch readiness. Cross-timezone syncs with Global Studio Content Services are a regular part of the rhythm – you'll bridge time zones and languages daily, ensuring nothing falls through the cracks between Tokyo and Los Angeles.

As the first hire in Japan, much of this role involves building — defining cadences, shaping workflows, and establishing the operational rhythm to meet launch expectations that will scale as the Japan Originals slate grows. You'll balance hands-on title management with the strategic work of building local Studio Content Services capabilities — addressing on-the-ground challenges, navigating local language dynamics with production teams and vendors, and providing dedicated in-market expertise that strengthens how Studio Content Services operates across the Japan slate.

About the team
Studio Content Services (SCS) owns all intake, management, and distribution operations for Amazon MGM Studios Originals globally — from defining deliverables with Post Production teams, to launching content on Prime Video, to managing assets through their full lifecycle including downstream licensing and preservation. We're a global team spanning LA, Singapore, and now Japan, operating at the intersection of creative and operations. Our culture values ownership, high standards, and trust — we move fast, solve hard problems collaboratively, and take pride in ensuring every title reaches customers at the highest quality.

This is the first dedicated hire in Japan, sitting at the intersection of Delivery, Localization, Content Operations, and PV Delivery Operations (PVDO) to serve as the local point of contact for all Studio Content Services functions. The role reports into the Global Delivery Manager in Singapore and partners closely with Global Studio Content Services in Los Angeles, bridging local production needs with Amazon's worldwide content operations. You'll be joining a team that's scaling rapidly to support a growing Japan Originals slate.

Basic qualifications

- Speak, write, and read fluently in Japanese
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English
- 6+ years of experience in content operations, digital supply chain, or post-production management within media/entertainment – including quality control and creation of domestic and international deliverables
- Experience managing multi-title content pipelines with concurrent delivery timelines
- Experience influencing multiple stakeholders and leading operational initiatives across multiple countries, time zones and languages
- Experience leading processes or workflow improvements or implementing operations processes or project management frameworks

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in team management and building (including coaching and mentoring)
- Knowledge of sound, dialogue, and music editing and mixing workflows
- Experience with Dolby Vision, Dolby Atmos, UHD, HDR, and film workflows
- Experience communicating and presenting to senior leadership
- Experience in a studio, production company or television network
- Established relationships with vendors for DI, sound, mastering, and QC
- Familiarity with the Japanese post-production and media services landscape

Our WW Operations network delivers millions of packages and smiles to Amazon customers every day. We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Operations Manager. In this role, you will lead and develop a team of salaried and hourly talent. title: Sr, Manager, UX/Design, Talent Acquisition-Tech
descriptionHtml:
Hiring is one of the most consequential decisions a person makes or receives, and the tools that power it are becoming genuinely agentic. We are seeking a Senior Manager of UX to lead the design and research organization behind our hiring portfolio at exactly this inflection point.

This is a rare leadership role. The products your team shapes increasingly act on behalf of the people who use them: drafting job descriptions, surfacing candidates, generating assessments, flagging risks, and moving work forward. The underlying systems are probabilistic. The experiences your team designs must not be. Your core challenge is building and leading a team that can translate AI systems operating on confidence, inference, and ranked signals into interactions that feel trustworthy, purposeful, and in control — where users understand what the system did, why, and what happens next.

You are a people leader with dual accountability: you own experience strategy across the full hiring portfolio, and you build the team, culture, and craft bar that make world-class work repeatable — not dependent on any one person. You partner as a peer with Principal Engineers, senior PMs, and Research and Product leaders from strategy through launch. You influence product direction and long-term business strategy, and you set the quality bar by developing the people and mechanisms that hold it.


Key job responsibilities
**Lead and grow the UX organization.** Build, structure, and develop a high-performing team of designers and researchers. Own hiring, org design, headcount planning, and resourcing across the portfolio. Set clear performance expectations, give direct and developmental feedback, manage performance, and actively drive career growth - including contributions to the promotion process. Recruit and raise the bar on talent.

**Own experience vision and strategy across the hiring portfolio.** Set the north star for Recruiter Hub, Hiring Hub, and Candidate Hub as a coherent, connected system - not three products. Define how users move between surfaces, how context transfers, and how the portfolio adds up to more than its parts. Lead this vision through your team rather than solely through your own hands.

**Define the agentic interaction model for hiring - through your team.** Own the strategy for experiences where AI acts on behalf of recruiters and hiring managers: delegation surfaces, approval flows, correction mechanisms, confidence transparency, and escalation paths. Establish the principles for when the system should act, when it should ask, and what trust looks like when it gets something wrong - and hold the team accountable to them.

**Establish scalable mechanisms and cross-product standards.** Create the interaction models, experience principles, design patterns, and measurement systems that govern AI-assisted hiring surfaces across the portfolio (e.g., UX/CX benchmarking, customer-frustration tracking, ongoing experience measurement). Ensure the system speaks one language at the human-AI boundary and that quality scales across partner teams rather than depending on heroics.

**Set and hold the design excellence bar.** Act as creative director for quality across the portfolio. Partner with and develop design and research leaders to raise the floor on visual craft, interaction quality, research rigor, and storytelling. Establish the review mechanisms and standards that make the bar visible and durable.

**Influence product and business direction.** Work with senior leadership to identify where design and research unlock product strategy, not just execute it. Bring recruiter, hiring manager, and candidate insight into roadmap decisions before requirements are written. Contribute to OP1/OP2 and 3-Year Plan (3YP) efforts, and be a named voice in strategic tradeoffs across major products and product suites.

**Own strategic communications.** Own research narratives, experience strategy documents, executive readouts, and quarterly status updates within and outside the organization. Make design and research rationale legible to non-designers and make the business case for quality to executive leadership.

**Drive rigor and delivery through the team.** Ensure the team uses research, behavioral data, and usability findings to diagnose the real problem before proposing solutions, and that specifications function as behavior contracts partners can build against. Ensure engineering partnership through delivery and close the gap between intent and reality.


A day in the life
You start your morning in a portfolio review - but you're not critiquing pixels, you're developing judgment. A designer walks through the AI-generated candidate summary feature; you name the three places where the model's uncertainty isn't surfaced and coach the team on why that matters for trust, so they catch it themselves next time. By mid-morning you're in a product strategy session with the PM and Principal Engineer on the Candidate Hub, where a roadmap capability threatens to fragment the experience into a fourth surface - you reframe the conversation and align leadership on the connected-system alternative.

In the afternoon you're working org problems: a hiring loop for a senior researcher, a career-development conversation with a design lead who's ready to grow, and a resourcing tradeoff across two teams competing for the same headcount. You end the day reviewing your team's craft bar - not to approve work, but to make sure the standard is visible, shared, and getting higher without you in the room.


About the team
Talent Solutions Product Design & Research designs the products that power how Amazon hires: the tools recruiters, hiring managers, interviewers, and candidates use across the full hiring journey. We own the end-to-end experience across the Recruiter Hub, Hiring Hub, and Candidate Hub, and we are at the leading edge of what it means to put AI into consequential, human-centered workflows.

We are building agentic products in a domain where trust is not optional. Our AI systems recommend, rank, predict, and increasingly act. Our design work determines whether people trust those systems enough to rely on them, understand them enough to correct them, and feel good enough about the experience to advocate for it. We are designers, researchers, and strategists who work backward from the people we serve, hold an unusually high bar for craft, and believe that the experience of being hired - or of hiring someone - matters.

- 10+ years of leading multi-discipline Design teams (ie. visual design, interaction design, user research, etc.) experience
- 5+ years of people management experience, including hiring, developing, and managing designers and/or researchers
- Experience owning experience strategy and setting the quality bar across multiple products or a product suite
- Experience partnering with senior Product, Engineering, and Research leaders to influence product and business strategy

Preferred qualifications

title: Senior Applied Scientist - Manipulation RL,  Amazon Robotics - Vulcan Stow
descriptionHtml:
Our organization in Amazon Robotics builds robots that perform contact-rich manipulation safely and reliably in complex, unstructured environments, at Amazon scale. Our scientists and engineers push the boundaries of robotic manipulation to handle enormous object diversity, bringing deep expertise across planning, control, perception, and machine learning. We learn from real-world data at a scale that few teams in robotics can access.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Applied Scientist to help guide a small team advancing reinforcement learning for manipulation. We are creating robots that learn how to push, flip, rearrange, and dexterously insert items with unparalleled robustness, speed, and reliability. Our goal is to deploy robots that will work across Amazon's global network and can handle the full diversity of items that Amazon sells. You will set the technical direction for how we learn these behaviors, from simulation training through reliable execution on physical robots, and you will demonstrate new manipulation capabilities on real hardware at scale. This team's mission reaches beyond any single product: to invent and apply manipulation capabilities that generalize to many future robotics applications. The robots our organization already deploys at scale give you a rare proving ground to collect data, run experiments, and get new policies onto real hardware faster than almost anywhere in the field. You will raise the bar for scientific rigor and engineering quality, and mentor other scientists as the team grows.

Key job responsibilities
- Set the technical direction for learning non-prehensile and contact-rich manipulation policies, from testing the latest advances in the field through demonstrated capability on hardware.
- Oversee the development of reinforcement learning approaches that address the long tail of diverse, demanding manipulation conditions.
- Own the path from simulation training to reliable, real-time execution on physical robots, making evidence based calls on where learned approaches should replace engineered ones.
- Demonstrate new manipulation capabilities on real robots at scale, and turn one-off results into repeatable methods.
- Establish the standards, evaluation practices, and data-informed improvement loops that the team builds on.
- Mentor scientists and engineers, and raise the bar for applied science rigor and engineering quality.
- Partner across control, perception, and hardware to integrate learned behaviors into working systems.
- Represent Amazon in academia through publications and scientific presentations.

descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we've designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

This role is for an experienced, self-directed individual who will work on development hardware to meet the needs of Amazon Leo. You'll partner directly with design engineers to iterate hardware quickly and qualify it for space, following that hardware through the full arc of development — initial prototyping, development builds, testing, and rigorous qualification testing — while working independently and seeking guidance only as needed. You'll also help shape the lab spaces themselves, adapting layout and equipment as designs change, and you'll begin sharing that expertise with teammates as the team grows. This is an R&D focused position covering the full range of hardware development lab support — assembly, troubleshooting, testing, equipment upkeep, and documentation — so expect the day-to-day to shift as project needs change.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
Work independently on ambiguous problems, seeking guidance from peers or management as needed
Partner directly with design engineers to iterate hardware quickly, optimize manufacturability, and qualify hardware for space
Support hardware through the full development arc — initial prototyping, development builds, testing, and rigorous qualification testing
Troubleshoot complex hardware and test setup issues, driving problems to root cause
Mechanical and electrical assembly of various spacecraft mechanisms
Engineer and adapt lab spaces and equipment to meet evolving customer needs, keeping labs clean, organized, and functioning well for their intended purpose, including tracking equipment calibrations
Design and build custom test fixtures, tooling, and automation equipment to support test and build needs
Develop and maintain clear engineering documentation, including work instructions, build notes, and test reports

Familiarity with aerospace/space quality standards for mechanical and electrical components

About the team
The Amazon Leo Development Operations (DevOps) team builds and maintains the labs and hardware infrastructure that let engineering teams design, prototype, and test satellite hardware quickly. We support projects from first prototype through qualification testing, and our team members cross-train across assembly, test, and lab equipment so we can flex to wherever the work is needed. Priorities shift fast as designs evolve, and you'll often move between projects to keep pace with what engineering teams need next. We take pride in keeping our labs and equipment in excellent shape, and we hold ourselves to a high standard because the hardware we build and test directly impacts what makes it to space.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of hardware development, test lab, space/aerospace maintenance or hands-on engineering environment experience
- Bachelor's degree or above in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, material science, physics or equivalent, or experience working in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM)
- Can lift up to 49 pounds, stand/walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, and be able to frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach

- Must be able to climb a ladder and work at heights above 6 feet
- May need to operate heavy equipment including overhead cranes and electric lifts. Rigging and hoisting tasks may be performed.
- Good vision, mental sharpness, alertness and function in confined spaces

Preferred qualifications

- Demonstrated expertise in a lab engineering domain (e.g., mechanical prototyping, electrical testing, environmental/qualification testing, or fixture design)

Du lernst, wie unsere Führungskräfte eine sichere, produktive Umgebung schaffen und das volle Potenzial ihrer Teams durch effektive Einbindung und Leistungsmanagement-Strategien nutzen. Das ist deine Chance, Fähigkeiten zu entwickeln, die dich zu einer lohnenden Karriere bei Amazon führen werden.

title: EHS Specialist
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon's mission to become Earth's safest place to work! At Amazon, we've set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. As a Workplace Health & Safety Specialist (WHSS), you'll be at the forefront of transforming workplace safety culture at one of the world's most innovative companies. Your expertise and dedication will directly protect employees, ensuring they return home safely to their families every day. You'll facilitate new approaches to safety, combining technology with human-centered solutions to create an environment where safety and productivity thrive together. This isn't just about maintaining safety standards – it's about revolutionizing how we think about and implement workplace safety, making a lasting impact on our people and operations. As your building's designated safety champion, you'll have the unique opportunity to build relationships, influence positive change, and help write the next chapter in Amazon's commitment to becoming Earth's Safest Place to Work. Core Impact Areas: Safety Program Excellence & Implementation - Drive comprehensive safety programs through data-driven strategies. Lead daily safety audits, incident investigations, and risk assessments while implementing innovative solutions to prevent injuries. Deliver engaging safety training that resonates with associates and promotes a proactive safety culture. Champion continuous improvement initiatives that enhance workplace safety while maintaining operational efficiency. Associate Advocacy & Cultural Leadership - Serve as a trusted safety advisor and advocate for associate wellbeing, building strong partnerships across all levels of the organization. Foster a culture where safety is everyone's priority through effective communication, coaching, and positive reinforcement. Develop strong relationships with frontline associates and leadership to drive behavioral changes and ensure safety best practices become natural habits. Transform safety data into compelling narratives that influence positive change and drive engagement in safety initiatives. Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)
- Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site
Must be available to work flexible shifts including days, nights and/or weekends.
For those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross, must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

Basic qualifications

- High school or equivalent
- A minimum of 1 year in an Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) related field OR; A Bachelor's degree in EHS-relevant background OR; 6 months experience performing in a safety-related role within Amazon
- Knowledge of OSHA regulations specifically 29 CFR 1910
- Experience using Microsoft Word and Excel in a professional capacity
- Experience maintaining confidentiality in matter involving security and/or personnel issues in the workplace

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or higher, preferably in a safety related field
- Strong communication, teamwork, analysis, judgment, and customer focus skills
- Experience leading and managing a team, ability to analyze accident data, new processes, and machinery for potential safety concerns, and conduct job hazard and job safety analyses
- Experience in emergency response and currently holds First Aid and CPR certificates
- Experience in workers compensation case management

title: Business Intelligence Engineer, Extended Producer Responsibility
descriptionHtml:
Are you energized by turning complex data into actionable insights that drive compliance and cost optimization at Amazon scale? If so, we'd like to talk to you.

As a Business Intelligence Engineer II on the WW EPR team, you will design, build, and maintain the data pipelines, reports, and analytics solutions that power our Worldwide EPR compliance and circularity programs. You will work with large, multi-regional datasets — delivering efficient, testable BI solutions that enable cross-functional teams to make data-driven decisions on regulatory obligations, recycling fees, and operational performance across global markets. You will collaborate directly with stakeholders and partner closely with senior BIEs to solve ambiguous problems, automate manual workflows, and continuously improve data quality and reporting standards.


Key job responsibilities
• Create mechanisms for non-technical stakeholders to self-serve data including during urgent issue management
• Scope and deliver strategic projects to accelerate the success of the safety programs supported
• Look for opportunities to simplify and automate redundant processes
• Take the problems of stakeholders and help them understand technical solutions which can be delivered
• Leverage a combination of AWS services, internal data services, and AI-based tooling and solutions to deliver data products and simplification

About the team
Our Worldwide EPR team owns Amazon's global compliance strategy for Extended Producer Responsibility — ensuring adherence to post-consumer waste regulations across packaging, electronics, batteries, and textiles in all operating regions. We enable circular economy value for Selling Partners, Vendors, and customers by connecting every product sold to verified recovery outcomes with auditable results. We work cross-functionally with Legal, Business, Product, and Data Science/Engineering teams across NA, EU, APAC, and emerging markets to deliver compliance programs at scale. EPR shifts post-consumer waste management costs from municipalities to producers — requiring all Selling Partners on Amazon's marketplace to register, report product data, pay recycling fees to PROs, and establish take-back systems. This incentivizes environmentally friendly product and packaging design.
EPR is part of the Regulatory Intelligence, Safety and Compliance (RISC) organization, dedicated to protecting Amazon customers from products that are illegal, unsafe, or otherwise prohibited

title: Cloud Hardware Development Engineer, AWS Hardware Engineering Services, Specialized Platforms and Servers
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) Hardware Engineering Services (HWEngS) owns the new product development (NPI) and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain, and we’re looking for talented people who want to help. You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers, and you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Cloud Hardware Development Engineer (CHDE): The Amazon Web Services (AWS) Hardware Engineering Services (HWEngS) Specialized Platforms and Servers team creates Enterprise rack solutions for Amazon’s innovative web services. We are seeking experienced CHDEs to own the fleet health, diagnostics, and automation of the Enterprise rack solutions:
1.) Designing and implementing predictive failure detection systems using telemetry, sensor data, error trends, and log correlation to identify hardware issues before they cause a customer impact.
2.) Driving toward zero-touch operations by building detection, diagnostics, and remediation of faults without human intervention
3.) Debugging complex system failures in time-sensitive settings personally diving deep when the problem demands it.
4.) Completing root cause analysis correlating across firmware, kernel, driver, thermal, power, and physical layers.

What you will do: As a member of the Specialized Platforms and Servers team, you’ll be responsible for collaborating with Elastic Cloud Compute (EC2) service teams and Data Center Operations to maintain fleet health in all the locations we have servers.

You will work closely with internal teams, suppliers, and external partners capturing lessons learned while operating the fleet to ensure next generation designs are of the highest quality, constantly looking for ways to improve your product performance, quality and cost.


Key job responsibilities
As a CHDE you will be responsible for scaling how we operate our massive existing & rapidly growing fleet. You will lead the integration and delivery of servers, support the development of automated monitoring, and failure analysis services to operate, debug, and scale our servers. You will work closely with other AWS software teams to tailor and operate servers solutions for the AWS environment. You will support launching our servers into production and operating our fleet of servers.

A day in the life
Your day to day responsibilities will be solving operational challenges to our existing fleet with the goal of improving the current customer experience as well as developing improved systems for future designs.

About the team
The team is comprised of CHDE's, System Development Engineers and Technical Program Managers, all with the common goal of delivering the best specialized server fleet possible to our customers.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.



Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or equivalent, or 3+ years of relevant technical position experience.
- 3+ years of experience in server level design for compute or other complex product design.
- Experience in developing design verification plans and functional test procedures.
- Experience in board and server root cause analysis and resolution.

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of experience in complex product development such as servers, network switches, or other highly integrated devices with hardware, software, and service aspects.
- Proficient scripting, debug abilities, and Linux operations commands.
- Experience deploying and operating hardware and applications across large data centers.
- Meets/exceeds Amazon’s leadership principles requirements for this role
- Meets/exceeds Amazon’s functional/technical depth and complexity for this role

title: Sr. Business Development Manager, Global Selling LatAm
descriptionHtml:
You will design and grow the partner network that brings Latin American businesses into selling on Amazon in the US — building something with regional reach and a direct line to measurable growth.

This role covers Mexico and Latin America. You'll build relationships with agencies, service providers, industry associations, and logistics companies, and turn those relationships into a sustainable, scalable channel for new seller recruitment.

Key job responsibilities
Design and execute the regional partner recruitment strategy: identify which types of organizations have the right relationships and client profile to bring new sellers to the US marketplace, and develop the approach for each category.

Build and develop partner relationships across Mexico and Latin America — understanding what drives each type of organization, what they value, and how to structure engagement that works for both sides long-term.

Develop the lead generation model: determine which channels, co-marketing formats, and outreach approaches grow the seller pipeline most effectively, and evolve the approach as the program scales.

Work across internal teams to ensure sellers entering the program are positioned for strong, sustained performance from day one.

Own program performance end-to-end: partner activity, pipeline health, seller quality, and revenue contribution. Know your numbers and act on them.

Continuously improve the model — operationally, commercially, and structurally — and bring well-reasoned proposals to leadership.

Shape the program's next phase: how to deepen partner engagement, which new categories and markets to enter, and what a more mature version of this program looks like.

A day in the life
The day starts with a read of the pipeline: which partners are active, where seller candidates are in the process, and what needs unblocking.

Mid-morning shifts to partner conversations — agencies, logistics firms, industry associations — assessing portfolio fit, co-designing outreach strategies, and aligning on what each organization needs to convert their clients into US expansion candidates.

The day closes on strategy: translating performance data into program decisions, preparing leadership proposals on market expansion, partner tiering, or new acquisition channels, and defining the next phase of growth.
