title: Robot Technician, RIVR
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a hands-on, resourceful, and detail-oriented Field Technician to support the maintenance, testing and operation of our advanced robotic systems. As a Field Technician, you will be responsible not only for preparing and maintaining the robotic platforms but also for representing our company in the field, adapting to unexpected challenges, and directly supporting testing with professionalism and technical expertise. As part of this role, you will also assist with production processes for the business and provide continuous improvement in terms of processes and instruction guides. For this position, we can unfortunately only accept applications from citizens of Schengen Area countries.

Key job responsibilities
● On-site Troubleshooting and First Response: Independently diagnose and resolve mechanical, electrical, and software issues, often under time pressure and changing conditions, utilizing established ticketing systems.
● Customer Interaction and Reporting: Serve as the technical point of contact for customers during field operations, providing clear communication, professional support, and post-mission reporting to internal teams.
● Data Collection and Reporting: Collect operational data, monitor system logs, and provide insights to engineering teams for system refinement.
● Preventive Maintenance and Inspection: Perform scheduled maintenance routines, visual inspections, and component replacements to maximize system uptime and extend hardware life.
● Production and Assembly Support: Assist with robot assembly, sub-system integration, and quality checks during production runs, ensuring builds meet engineering specifications.
● Process Documentation and Continuous Improvement: Create, update, and refine work instructions, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and deployment checklists based on field learnings and evolving best practices.
● Inventory and Spare Parts Management: Track spare parts, consumables, and tooling; coordinate restocking and ensure field kits are complete and deployment-ready.
● Safety and Compliance: Uphold workplace health and safety standards across workshop and field environments, including proper handling of batteries, electrical systems, and heavy equipment.
● Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with software, hardware, and operations engineers to relay field observations, validate fixes, and support iterative design improvements.
● Test Execution and Validation: Support structured testing campaigns—both in the lab and in the field—by following test protocols, recording results, and flagging anomalies for engineering review.


About the team
RIVR is a Swiss robotics company pioneering Physical AI and robotic solutions to revolutionize last-mile delivery, giving 1 human the power of 1000. Through the combination of artificial neural networks and innovative robot designs with wheels and legs, RIVR aims to enhance efficiency, sustainability, and scalability in last-mile delivery. Founded as Swiss-Mile, the company rebranded to RIVR in 2025 to better reflect its mission of driving the future of intelligent robotics. Join our innovative team, renowned for pioneering robotic design and neural network applications in robotics that improve environmental understanding and decision-making. With a robust research foundation and notable contributions from ETH Zurich, we are leaders in translating artificial intelligence and robotics into practical, real-world applications.
RIVR is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team that values every perspective. If you’re passionate about driving innovation in robotics and creating meaningful impact, we encourage you to apply and bring your unique self to our team.

Basic qualifications

- Experience in customer-facing work, engaging with customer executives, technologists or partners to solve business problems with advanced technologies
- Degree or apprenticeship in mechatronics, robotics, or equivalent.
- Proven ability to work independently in the field, diagnose problems under pressure, and perform quick, effective repairs without immediate supervision.
- Ability to follow structured procedures, deployment checklists, safety protocols, and quality standards even in dynamic environments.
- Willingness and ability to travel to field locations - sometimes on short notice. Interest in both maintaining and operating robotics systems.

Preferred qualifications

title: Software Development Engineer, AWS Security Epoxy
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Security operates at a scale few engineers ever get to work at. Epoxy is the team that builds the automation making that coverage possible. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to support the building and operating of the platforms that onboard threat detection, remediate security risk, and accelerate security response across every AWS account.

AWS Security, Epoxy builds a collection of automation platforms for AWS Security. We enable threat detection across a large fleet of AWS accounts (onboarding coverage, auditing it continuously, and making findings available to partner teams), we help partner teams remediate detected risks and respond to incidents automatically at scale, and we run the foundational services (communications, workflow orchestration, data enrichment, and secure access) that the rest of AWS Security][ operations relies on. Our systems operate at very high scale and carry a high operational bar: you build it, you run it.

You are a Software Development Engineer who enjoys taking a difficult, loosely specified problem and turning it into a well designed, thoroughly tested, and cleanly operated system. You care about the quality of what you ship and about leaving the systems you touch better than you found them. Experience in security is a plus, but it is not a requirement: what matters most is that you build robust, maintainable, high quality software using modern practices and technologies such as AWS services, Python, and TypeScript, and that you take ownership of the operational health of what you deliver.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and deliver features and components that solve difficult problems across AWS Security Epoxy's services, working independently from a well understood business goal even when the implementation is not fully specified.
- Own the operational excellence of the systems you work on: instrument them, alarm on the right signals, and drive down operational load through automation rather than manual toil.
- Write high quality, well tested code that meets a high engineering bar, and clear documentation and runbooks that let others maintain and extend your work.
- Participate in the team on-call rotation, supporting our services and responding to high-severity requests from AWS Security operations and Partner Teams. You resolve issues, then eliminate their contributing causes with permanent fixes.
- Improve the resiliency, scalability, and safety of systems that operate at very high scale, making sound trade-offs between short-term needs and long-term maintainability.
- Raise the bar through code reviews, design reviews, operational readiness reviews, and post-incident analyses, giving useful and actionable feedback including to more senior engineers.
- Mentor newer teammates and interns, and begin to influence partner teams by helping them adopt sound engineering and operational practices.

A day in the life
You pick up a feature request on one of Epoxy's services, break it into deliverable pieces, and ship it incrementally with tests and monitoring in place.

You review a teammate's design, ask the questions that surface a hidden resiliency risk, and help simplify the approach before code is written.

On an on-call week, you triage a high-severity issue, mitigate customer impact quickly, then open the follow-up work to make sure that class of failure cannot recur.

You spot a piece of manual operational work your team repeats every week and replace it with automation, giving the whole team time back.

You sync with a partner detection or response team to understand how they use an Epoxy capability, and feed what you learn back into the roadmap.

title: Head of Programming Strategy, Prive Video Japan
descriptionHtml:
Prime Video is seeking a Head of Japan Programming Strategy to own the end-to-end programming strategy for one of Prime Video's largest and most strategically important streaming markets. Japan is a priority locale with a deep local slate, a distinctive competitive landscape, and globally significant content categories — most notably Anime — that reach audiences far beyond the domestic market.
This is a senior, strategy-led leadership role with a mandate to innovate. Its center of gravity is insights-led, forward-looking slate health planning — not just day-to-day scheduling. Your team will decide what Japan should be programming and investing in over the next 3–5 years and why, using audience and performance insights to steer the slate. Equally important, you will look for new ways to expand the reach of Japan programming — new audiences, categories, formats, and distribution and promotional approaches — and reinvent how the team works internally, adopting automation and AI-assisted tooling so the team spends its time on strategy rather than routine execution.
You will be the single-threaded owner for Japan programming, leading a team based in Japan and operating with a high degree of autonomy while ensuring Japan's work is tightly aligned to Global and APAC-wide mechanisms, standards, and priorities.


Key job responsibilities
Own the Japan programming strategy, weighted toward insights-led slate decisions — moving the team from "what airs when" to "what we should invest in and why."
Find new ways to expand the reach of Japan programming — identifying new audiences, categories, formats, and promotional and distribution approaches that grow engagement beyond the current slate and surface Japanese content to wider domestic and global audiences.
Innovate how the team works internally — reinventing programming workflows, mechanisms, and tooling (including automation and AI-assisted approaches) so the team shifts its time from routine reporting and coordination toward high-value strategy and insight.
Own slate health as a portfolio — balancing genres, categories, and title types to sustain engagement and retention, and proactively identifying gaps and over-indexes before they affect performance.
Map the Japan slate on a 3–5 year horizon, not just near-term calendar planning — enabling earlier, better-informed content and investment decisions and tighter alignment to global title strategy.
Drive rapid strategic pivots, re-orienting Japan's programming priorities and long-range strategic direction quickly as market dynamics, competitive moves, or global signals shift.
Fill calendar and slate gaps with hub programming solutions, drawing on APAC regional and global content (imports, worldwide categories such as Anime, cross-locale titles) to turn gaps into growth opportunities.
Lean into Anime and title-travelability ownership, aligning the team on travelability to drive measurable improvement in local Anime performance.
Partner cross-functionally — with Content/Studios, Marketing, Product, Customer Insights, Business Intelligence, and Finance — to align programming with launch, campaign, and business goals.
Define and track the KPIs that measure programming and slate-health effectiveness for Japan, and own regular performance reporting and the quarterly slate-health plan-of-record.


About the team
Prime Video Japan is one of Prime Video's largest and most strategically important markets in Global, with a deep local slate, a passionate and distinctive audience, and globally significant content categories — most notably Anime — that resonate far beyond Japan. The Japan programming team shapes what Japanese customers watch and discover, combining strong local expertise with a direct connection to regional and global programming initiatives. As Head of Japan Programming Strategy, you will lead a team as it evolves from an execution-focused group into a strategy-led, innovation-minded organization — deepening its use of audience insights, owning the long-range health of the Japan slate, finding new ways to grow programming reach, and reinventing how the team works day to day.

Basic qualifications

- Experience in managing and developing teams
- Bachelor's degree in a relevant field or equivalent work experience
- Speak, write, and read fluently in Japanese at a business level or above (N1+)
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English
- 10+ years of experience in programming, content strategy, slate planning, or a closely related media/streaming/strategy planning discipline.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in audience segmentation and targeting
- Experience working with global and cross-functional teams across business development, marketing, operations, product development and legal
- Experience influencing multiple stakeholders and leading cross functional teams across geographies and business units
- Experience with long-range (multi-year) content or slate strategy, not solely near-term scheduling.
- Deep familiarity with the Japan media/entertainment market and audience.

title: Controls Engineer, Deployment, CDS - DCCD
descriptionHtml:
As part of the global controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for troubleshooting, project management, and maintaining the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS). Using Amazon leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space. AWS Data centers have multiple components such as generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers [air-cooled and water-cooled], pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers, etc. All these components have local control systems that interact with each other via open and/or proprietary communications protocols. The BMS is the primary method of control of all mechanical systems within a data center. The EPMS is the primary method of monitoring all electrical systems within a data center.

Key job responsibilities
Train and assist internal customers and stakeholders with the creation, design, configuration, validation, installation, commissioning and operation of BMS and EPMS systems.

Provide technical assistance and support to operations during life cycle of the data center. Review results and action items from the quarterly maintenances for BMS and EPMS and take actions to get them resolved.

Develop BMS & EPMS projects scope of work, schedule, budget, and level of efforts (LOE) to projects requested by customers and stakeholders.

Manage scope, schedule, finance and execution of BMS and EPMS improvement projects in AWS data centers.

Assist in procurement related activities including request for quotation/proposals, responding to request for information, review of vendors proposal and issuance of purchase orders.

Participate in AWS global on-call schedule to provide immediate BMS and EPMS technical support to in-service data centers.

Attend project related meetings, coordinate with project leaders and regularly report status to Controls and stakeholders’ management.

Support Controls projects related commissioning activities in the data centers.

Review, implement, troubleshoot and iterate on the controls sequence of operation (SOO) and provide necessary feedback to the design team.

Develop and modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces.

Manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements and navigate challenging situations.

Financially manage BMS and EPMS service contracts.

Frequently visit (locally) assigned in-operation and/or under construction data centers to troubleshoot, meet customers, supervise vendor’s work to ensure compliance with the scope, design, SOO and applicable local codes.

A day in the life
As a Data Center Controls Engineer, your primary customers are Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO), who depend on you to deliver reliable, well integrated Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS). The problems you solve are technical: modifying controls logic to address operational issues, developing Methods of Procedure (MOPs) for firmware upgrades, or investigating complex alarm discrepancies across monitoring systems. For new builds, you own the controls scope from vendor submittal review through commissioning and turnover. You manage vendor relationships, budgets, and schedules for both service contracts and capital projects. Your internal stakeholders include your Controls Manager, Controls Technicians you provide technical direction to, and partner teams (Construction, Critical Projects Implementation, Commissioning, DCEO).

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering, or 5+ years of relevant discipline work experience
- 3+ years of relevant work in a data center or other critical environment experience
- 2+ years of vendor management experience
- 2+ years of construction or project management experience

Preferred qualifications

- CFC license or PMI qualification (PMP, IPMA, IPMC)

title: Sr. Security Engineer, Leo Security
descriptionHtml:
We are open to hiring candidates to work out of one of the following locations:

Redmond, WA, USA

Leo is an initiative to launch a constellation of Low Earth Orbit satellites that will provide low-latency, high-speed broadband network connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world.

Have you wanted an opportunity to secure an advanced satellite based broadband telecom service? The Leo Security team owns the security of product and operations of Leo end-to-end. We provide the necessary infrastructure and mechanisms to ensure the security of our satellite constellation and to protect the integrity and confidentiality of our customer data. Our team drives the research & development, deployment and operation of several mission-critical security systems and mechanisms. You will work in a start-up like environment, backed by Amazon’s infrastructure to bootstrap security mechanisms, and help instill the security culture in the organization.

Export Control Requirement

Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
You and your team own the vulnerability management program for Leo systems across a large and heterogeneous fleet. The discovery, prioritization, and remediation actions themselves run on Amazon-wide mechanisms; your responsibility is to make sure those mechanisms actually work for Leo's unique fleet requirements, that coverage and risk-based prioritization hold up against how our systems are really built, and that gaps get closed. You will drive resolution of the high-severity and systemic vulnerabilities that matter most by coordinating across the teams that own them, and you will lead the burn down of long-term technical debt and risk so the fleet gets measurably safer over time.

You will be a guardian for security simplicity. Leo's builders should inherit security at scale in ways that are easy to consume and that do not pile on untold burden or distract from shipping a game-changing satellite internet service, and it is your job to make sure that promise holds. You will collect feedback from the builders living with these mechanisms, detect where security is becoming friction instead of a default, and push to simplify it, so that doing the secure thing stays the path of least resistance rather than a tax on building.

You will partner with builder teams and their leaders as a trusted advisor, helping them understand their risk, define security priorities, and secure their systems without slowing their delivery. You will assess technical debt and risk alongside them, provide strategic direction that addresses vulnerabilities and fortifies our products, help leaders measure their organization's security execution, and guide teams toward outcomes that produce products which safely handle customer data. Beyond any single engagement, you will instill a security culture that makes secure practices a default rather than an afterthought, and you will mentor builders who aspire to become security advocates and security engineers through 1-1 sessions and office hours, growing the next generation of security talent across the organization.

You will translate compliance and regulatory requirements into concrete, auditable engineering controls and evidence, keeping Leo continuously audit-ready rather than scrambling before each review. You will define and report the metrics that show whether the program is working, including coverage, time-to-remediate, SLA adherence, and residual risk, and you will use that data to drive decisions.

A day in the life
In this highly dynamic role, you will join a team that is collectively accountable for where our security investments deliver the most value and most simplify security for Leo's builders. Together you will decide where to focus, challenge each other's priorities, and share the hard problems rather than carry them alone. No two days look the same, and the judgment the team brings to where it spends its attention is at the heart of the job.

Teams will reach out for ideas on how to handle a wide variety of security problems, and you will be the person they trust to point them at the right answer. You can anticipate implementation questions like "What is the paved path for vulnerability management?", "This finding is flagged on my service but I think it is a false positive, how do I confirm it?", "I have a patch SLA I cannot meet without downtime, what are my options?", or "How do I keep this class of vulnerability from coming back?" You will help them cut through the noise, understand what actually matters for their systems, and get unblocked without slowing their delivery.

When you are not responding to builder teams, you will step back and evaluate overall org performance to find the architectural defects behind recurring findings. Rather than chasing each ticket, you will look for the pattern underneath: a misconfiguration that keeps reappearing across the fleet, a dependency that drags a whole class of services below the bar, a gap in coverage where risk is going undetected. You will propose new security scanning capability and threat detections to close those gaps, and you will push to fix problems at the source so they stop generating work for everyone downstream.

You will spend time in the data, reading the metrics that tell you whether the program is actually working: where remediation is stalling, which teams are trending the wrong way, where an SLA is about to slip, and where residual risk is concentrating. You will turn that signal into action, whether that means tuning how Amazon-wide mechanisms apply to Leo's fleet, driving a targeted campaign to burn down a specific risk, or raising a systemic issue to the leaders who own it. When a high-severity or systemic vulnerability lands, you will coordinate the response across every team that owns a piece of it and drive it to closure.

Through all of it, you will help Amazon maintain a high bar for customer security. Every mechanism you tune, every gap you close, and every builder you unblock adds up to a fleet that is measurably safer and a security experience that stays simple enough that builders can keep shipping.

In this role, you will partner with business leaders to deliver HR initiatives focused on talent management, employee engagement, and internal customer service. Success requires leveraging data-driven insights and understanding the importance of HR metrics to drive business impact. You may also lead a team of entry-level HR employees and own projects that enhance the employee experience.

title: Data Center Chief Engineer, Data Center Engineering Operation
descriptionHtml:
As Chief Engineer, you will be responsible for ensuring that all electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment within the data center is operating at peak efficiency. This involves planned preventative maintenance of equipment, daily corrective work, and emergency response. You are expected to be a singular focal point for all facility operations and to support Amazon within its owned and operated data centers.

You should be able to manage large scale impacting projects and new region support from conception to completion. These projects involve large amounts of independent work as well as collaboration with external support groups including engineering, automation, procurement, and finance in both local and global settings. As Chief Engineer, you will be tasked with creating and delivering on key milestones, obtaining and tracking quotes for all necessary costs, and documenting project results for future implementation at other facilities. The goals of such projects are for the Chief Engineers to drive innovation and resiliency while reducing operational costs in the facilities.

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

The Worldwide Sustainability (WWS) organization capitalizes on Amazon’s scale, speed, ability to build, invent, and simplify a resilient and sustainable company. We manage our social and environmental impacts globally, and drive solutions that enable our customers, businesses, and the world to become more sustainable.

• Work at height, and from ladders

- Execution of project scopes of basic complexity
- Providing timely escalation for all facilities-related issues within the data center

title: Principal Technical Program Manager, Fauna
descriptionHtml:
Fauna Robotics is building capable, safe, and delightful robots for everyday life. We are hiring a Principal Technical Program Manager to lead how robot software ships at Fauna. Our products improve with each software release: new features and skills make robots already in the hands of developers and partners more useful.

In this role, you will own the software release program end-to-end, from planning to deployment. This includes how we move research into the product, how hardware changes are reflected in software, and how we deliver a great software experience to customers. You will build the planning mechanisms for the software organization, drive excellence in execution, and lead our largest launches

Key job responsibilities
- Own the robot software release program: cadence, go/no-go criteria, staged rollouts, and rollback decisions

- Collaborate with hardware, firmware, science, and manufacturing programs so that robot software is ready to ship on time and with high quality

- Build roadmaps, dependency tracking, and status reporting for the software org and own the integration plan for major launches and demos

- Define release quality bars with QA and engineering, and use test results, telemetry, and field reports to decide when to ship

- Set the multi-year plan for how Fauna ships robot software as the fleet and the org grow, and build mechanisms for the long term

- Find problems that recur across teams and fix the process that causes them, and handle escalations as they happen across the program

- Present program status, risks, and tradeoffs to senior leadership

About the team
Fauna Robotics, an Amazon company, is building capable, safe, and genuinely delightful robots for everyday life. Our goal is simple: make robots people actually want to live and interact with in everyday human spaces.

We believe that future won't arrive until building for robotics becomes far more accessible. Today, too much effort is spent reinventing the fundamentals. We're changing that by developing tightly integrated hardware and software systems that make it faster, safer, and more intuitive to create real-world robotic products.

Our work spans the full stack: mechanical design, control systems, dynamic modeling, and intelligent software. The focus is not just functionality, but experience. We're building robots that feel responsive, expressive, and genuinely useful.

At Fauna, you'll work at the frontier of this space, helping define how robots move, manipulate, and interact with people in natural environments. It's an opportunity to solve hard problems across hardware and software with a team focused on making robotics accessible and joyful to build.

If you care about making robotics real for everyone and building systems that are as delightful as they are capable, we're interested in hearing from you.

Basic qualifications

- 7+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 10+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- 5+ years of software development experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience leading software release programs for products that run on physical devices, such as robots, vehicles, consumer electronics, or connected home devices
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience

Preferred qualifications

- Experience bringing machine learning models from research into a shipping product
- Experience aligning software releases with hardware development stages (EVT, DVT, PVT)
- Experience with release engineering, CI/CD, or hardware-in-the-loop testing
- Experience running releases for developer-facing products such as SDKs or APIs
- Experience with over-the-air update delivery and staged fleet rollouts

title: Senior Product Designer, Prime Video
descriptionHtml:
Are you interested in shaping the future of entertainment? Do you want to define the next generation of how and what Amazon customers are watching?

Prime Video is changing the way people watch movies and TV. From one service, we're delivering versatile ways to watch hundreds of thousands of movies, TV series, and live events on the web, mobile, and TV. Our service is available in 240+ territories globally, and we're just getting started.

Working closely with business and technology partners, we use research, design, and prototyping to guide early product development, bring clarity to engineering goals, and develop a customer-centric point of view.
This is where you come in. As a Senior Product Designer, you'll join our Enterprise team within Prime Video Experience Design and lead design for a suite of products that uses AI to plan, manage, and optimize Prime Video's marketing at scale. The ambition is a progressively hands-off-the-wheel experience: a system that learns from every campaign, recommends the categorization, tiering, budget, channels, and creative that will move engagement, and takes on more of the planning and execution over time so people supervise and decide rather than assemble. This is a suite rather than a single product, and much of it is being defined now. You'll own the design direction across it, from framing problems that nobody has framed yet through detailed interaction design, developer handoff, launch, and what we learn afterwards.

The hard part is not the automation. It is the judgement around it. When a system can plan and produce more than any person can check, the design problem becomes how someone trusts it: what they see to make a decision quickly, where confidence, provenance, and the reasoning behind a recommendation surface, how they correct rather than reject, and what happens when the system is wrong. A hands-off-the-wheel experience only works if the human can see what the machine is about to do, understand why, step in at the right altitude, and stay accountable for the outcome.

You'll co-own that behavior with engineering, and you'll set the line for the team on where the system can drive and where a human still has to. If designing for probabilistic systems and the trust, control, and recovery they demand is the work you want to be doing, there is a great deal of unsolved ground here.

You'll establish the interaction and visual standards that hold this portfolio together, and build the patterns and mechanisms that make the designers around you faster. You'll use AI-assisted design workflows to move quickly, from rapid prototyping through to designing generative and agentic AI capabilities into the products themselves.

You'll partner closely with Product Management, Engineering, UX Research, Design Technology, and the marketing, brand, creative, sports, and portfolio teams who depend on this work, taking a clear position and arguing for it in writing and in the room. You'll be surrounded by senior designers, researchers, and design technologists working the same domain, on problems complex enough to build real depth in.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead end-to-end design across a suite of AI-driven marketing planning, management, and optimization products, from problem framing through handoff, launch, and iteration
- Design toward a progressively hands-off-the-wheel experience: define the levels of automation, what the system does on its own versus what it proposes for approval, and how that boundary moves as trust is earned
- Co-own the AI behavior with engineering: how people trust recommendations, see the reasoning and provenance behind them, review at volume, correct rather than reject, and recover when the system is wrong
- Design the intelligence layer that closes the loop, connecting strategy, goals, spend, and outcomes so the system learns from every campaign and surfaces benchmarks and recommendations that drive the next one
- Design AI-assisted and increasingly automated planning across the campaign lifecycle: categorization and tiering across territories, budget and channel allocation, work-back and scheduling, team assignment, and the brief
- Design the AI creative capabilities within the suite: generating marketing assets at scale, and the review, correction, and quality bar that make generated output shippable
- Define where the system's output, from a recommended plan to a generated asset, is good enough to ship and where human craft and human decision are still required
- Map the full marketing lifecycle across formats, languages, and territories, and design for its real constraints: scale, variants, multi-team processes, and edge cases
- Set the interaction and visual standards that give the portfolio coherence, and feed them back into our design system
- Lead workstreams with other designers, and build the patterns and tooling that make them faster
- Tie design decisions to measurable outcomes, and prioritize ruthlessly
- Present and defend recommendations to senior leadership, and write the narratives that move decisions without you in the room
- Partner across product, engineering, research, design technology, marketing, brand, sports, portfolio, legal, and data science
- Run discovery with the marketers, strategists, channel owners, portfolio planners, and operators doing this work today
- Mentor the designers around you and raise the team's practice

About the team
You'll be joining the Enterprise team within Prime Video Experience Design. We design the tools and workflows used by the content partners, marketers, operators, and internal teams who power the Prime Video content supply chain. Our products span marketing planning and portfolio management, channel strategy, campaign execution, marketing creative production, partner-facing content management, content acquisition, partner onboarding, publishing, and analytics. GenAI is the connective tissue across all of it, changing both what we deliver and how we deliver it, and moving these tools from systems people operate toward systems that increasingly plan and act on their own. We've built an enterprise design system that brings coherence and quality to a growing portfolio of tools. We're scrappy but detail-oriented, and we know when to move fast versus when to dive deep. We work alongside UX Researchers and Design Technologists, and our enterprise customers are close enough to test what we build and tell us what needs to change.

Basic qualifications

- 8+ years of design experience
- Have an available online portfolio
- Experience with design tools such as Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign and prototyping in HTML, JavaScript, CSS, Ajax

Preferred qualifications

- Experience applying scrum to visual or UX design processes
- Experience with UX design of complex workflows

title: Data Center Engineering Operations Cluster Manager, DCC Communities
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, we're working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. Join this highly visible team in a highly visible role.

The ATL Cluster is a fast growing region with many growth opportunities. Don't hesitate to reach out about this highly impactful, highly visible role.

The Infrastructure Operations organization is looking for an extraordinary individual with proven and tested leadership and management skills as a leader in our facilities operations organization in Atlanta as a Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO) Cluster Manager.

DCEO Cluster Manager is one of our most senior management roles in Atlanta. In this role, you will be responsible for leading a large organization, managing Area Managers and/or Facility Managers who own data center facility infrastructure. In other words, DCEO Cluster Manager is ultimately in charge of managing multiple data centers.
The pace, scale, and growth of Amazon’s data center platform will challenge you. Our uncompromisingly high standards as we continually seek to innovate on behalf of our customers will push you to new levels of creativity. At this level Amazon is unique in that we seek experienced senior leaders who have evolved to be highly strategic in their approach to managing their business unit, yet understand how to lead large teams by example who will not hesitate to roll up their sleeves when tactical needs dictate it.

The ideal candidate for this role will have a strong understanding in data center/mission critical MEP infrastructure. You will be the single point of the contact for all facility related issues from Atlanta team and work as the technical resource to support Regional Cluster Manager. You will solely be responsible for maintaining 100% service uptime in your Cluster. You have a very high-level view of your organization but you will need to deep dive into details as needed. You will also be interacting with global team on a daily basis by representing Atlanta Data Center Engineering Operations team.

If you are passionate about the Customer Experience, think and act globally and want to contribute to the operational excellence of Amazon.com data centers. This may be the challenge you’ve been looking for!

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

- 5+ years of general contractor and vendor management work (request for proposals, bidding, change orders, quality control, RFI/submittal tracking) associated with construction and project execution experience

title: Product Designer, Amazon Music Design, Amazon Music Design
descriptionHtml:
Everyone on our team has a meaningful impact on product features, new directions in music streaming, and customer engagement. As we continue to grow, we are looking for a talented and passionate UX Designer to play a vital role in shaping the products and services for Amazon Music. Our ideal candidate has the ability to delight customers with their user-centered product design work, by solving customers’ problems and tapping into customers’ love and passion for music.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead UX design for projects across platforms that touch numerous aspects of the Amazon Music experience.
- Run the full experience design process (i.e., discovery, research, concept development, wireframes, high-fidelity mocks) with a particular focus on customer mindsets, complex interaction solutions, user flows, and end-to-end customer journeys.
- Work from high-level requirements, ask the right questions, and collaborate with cross-functional partners to gather all relevant information to guide design direction.
- Quickly iterate on multiple design explorations to arrive at simple, but robust solutions, accounting for complex requirements.
- Validate designs through research and testing.
- Design for current experiences while also envisioning and creating new experiences for future features.
- Stay current on emerging UX and digital behavior trends, music and design innovations, and broader technological shifts, as well as identify opportunities to incorporate best current thinking into product designs.
- Collaborate on and present work to a range of stakeholders – executives, engineers, product managers, business leaders, researchers, other UX and visual designers.

A day in the life
As UX Designer on this team, you will help define, build, and deliver customer-facing experiences and tools, as well as delightful fan experiences from discovery and research to concept development, wireframes, and high-fidelity cross-platform mocks. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams across the organization, working from high-level requirements to define product design flows, interactions, and content strategies. You will incorporate best current thinking into product designs, while also envisioning and creating new experiences for future features. To be successful you must be collaborative, customer-focused problem solver with clear design chops, an excitement for applying data, and an ability to communicate your ideas effectively. Being a big music fan is a plus.

About the team
Amazon Music is an immersive audio entertainment service that deepens connections between fans, artists, and creators. From personalized music playlists to exclusive podcasts, concert livestreams to artist merch, Amazon Music is innovating at some of the most exciting intersections of music and culture. We offer experiences that serve all listeners across different tiers of service. Join us for the opportunity to influence how Amazon Music engages fans, artists, and creators on a global scale.

- Experience working in a collaborative team and working directly with developers for implementation of designs

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of mass-market consumer web / mobile products experience
- Experience guiding or managing user research and usability testing

title: Senior Real Estate Contract Manager, Japan Real Estate
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Japan Real Estate (JPRE)は成長を続けるAmazon Japanにおいて、カスタマーのニーズに応える全体最適な物流ネットワークを支える物流拠点の調達およびの運用を担うチームであり、グローバル組織であるGlobal Operations Enterprise Services (GOES)に所属しています。このたびJPRE内のReal Estate Contract Management部門 (RECM)にて、Sr.Real Estate Contract Managerを募集します。本ポジションは、定型的な契約管理・システム運用・支払処理といった基礎業務を自律的にこなしたうえで、より難易度の高い契約交渉・プロセス改善・チームへの貢献をリードする役割を担います。

このポジションの魅力

不動産、財務、経理、法務、施設管理など多様なチームと連携しながら、Amazonの物流ネットワーク全体を支える不動産契約管理の中核を担います。拠点の新設・拡張・統合・解約まで、不動産ライフサイクルの全ステップを経験できる環境です。グローバル組織であるGlobal Operations Enterprise Servicesの一員として、国際的な視点でのキャリア形成も可能です。

Key job responsibilities
契約管理・システム運用
- 複雑なリース契約書のレビューと重要情報の抽出・分析
- 契約条件のニュアンスを理解し、コスト最適化の機会を特定
- リース管理システム（Tango）への登録・更新を主体的に管理
- 覚書・通知書等の契約変更書類のレビューとシステム反映
- 社内外からの問い合わせ対応（エスカレーション含む）
契約期日管理
- リース契約の満了時期・更新期限・修正契約の賃料開始日等の重要期日を自律的に追跡・管理
- 関係者への期日案内による更新漏れ・満了見落としの防止
- 複数拠点にまたがる契約期日の優先順位付けと管理
支払処理・財務連携
- 敷金・家賃・駐車場・光熱費等の月次支払処理を社内規程に沿って実行
- 財務部・経理部との連携による正確かつ適時の支払実現
- 転貸契約の管理および入金処理
- 支払承認前の事前確認とアドバイスによる問題の未然防止
- チームの支払処理パフォーマンス指標の作成・管理
予算管理・コンプライアンス
- 適切な予算確保と支払遅延・契約違反の防止
- 社内支払規程およびリース契約条件の遵守
- 内外の規制監査コンプライアンスのサポート
業務改善・グローバル連携
- 契約管理システムの機能向上プロジェクトへの積極的な参画
- グローバルチームとの協働によるシステム改善の推進
- 業務プロセスの改善機会の発見と効率化の実現
- 契約管理プロセスの標準化・最適化への貢献
- チームのベストプラクティスを適用・共有し、他メンバーへの指導を開始
ステークホルダー管理
- 社外パートナー（賃貸人、不動産会社、駐車場契約先）および社内チームとの連携

- シニアリーダーへのエスカレーションを適切に判断・実行

A day in the life
業務割合（目安）：
[25%] 新規契約関連：契約書レビュー、サプライヤー口座開設、システム登録
[30%] 既存契約関連：契約満了時期の案内、覚書レビュー、変更情報の整理とシステム反映、情報管理

title: Sr. Conversational AI Product Design Technologist , Prime Video
descriptionHtml:
Are you interested in shaping the future of entertainment? Do you want to shape the next generation of the Amazon Prime Video's content discovery and viewing experience? Prime Video is changing the way people watch movies and TV. From one service, we're delivering versatile ways to watch hundreds of thousands of movies, TV series, and live events on the web, mobile, and TV. Our service is available in more than 200 territories globally, and we're just getting started.

Working closely with business and technology partners, we use research, design, and prototyping to explore the frontier of generative AI and conversational experiences, guide early product development, and develop a customer-centric point of view.

As a Conversational AI Product Design Technologist, you'll be a key part of our UX design organization. Your role will be all about proving, advancing, and evolving cutting-edge conversational experiences through prototyping and hands-on product work. You'll translate human conversational needs into AI interaction behaviors, and you'll build what you design, writing system instructions, shaping model behavior, building evaluations, and prototyping across platforms. We welcome candidates who come at this from design technology, UX research, linguistics, or IVR backgrounds, and we value a deep instinct for conversation paired with real AI fluency.

Key job responsibilities
-Build high-quality, functional prototypes that convey and advance the vision of future conversational experiences.

-Translate human conversational needs into AI interaction behaviors, balancing a natural and trustworthy voice.

-Shape model behavior by writing and refining system instructions and prompts, building goldens and platinums, and partnering on reinforcement learning and evaluations.

-Design and build for repair and recovery, handling ambiguity, misunderstanding, hallucination, and graceful failure.

-Define conversational quality metrics and apply them to measurably improve the experience, including building LLM-as-a-judge evaluations.

-Prototype across voice, text, visual, and ambient (multimodal) surfaces, using the best and most appropriate tools for the task.

-Collaborate with design leadership and stakeholders throughout the product lifecycle, and work alongside designers, researchers, PMs, and engineers to drive concepts from idea to implementation.

-Thrive in a fast-paced, iterative environment with ambiguous challenges and brand new customer experiences.

A day in the life
One moment you might be mapping how a conversation should recover when a customer is misunderstood, then writing the system instructions that get the model there and standing up an evaluation to measure whether it holds up. The next moment, you might be building an interactive prototype on AWS Bedrock to show partners and leadership what the experience feels like, directing the model the way a film director uses analogies rather than spot correcting, letting it apply its own reasoning and world knowledge to interpret intent. You will move fluidly between designing the experience, shaping the model, and coding the prototype that makes it real.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of front-end technologist, engineer, or UX prototyper experience
- An available online portfolio, with coding or prototyping samples that demonstrate conversational AI work.
- Hands-on experience prototyping with and designing for LLM-powered products.
- Experience shaping AI systems, including writing system instructions and prompts and building or running evaluations.
- Experience building functional prototypes, for example with front-end technologies, AI prototyping tools, or AWS tools such as Bedrock.

Preferred qualifications

- Background in UX Design, UX research, linguistics, computational linguistics, or IVR/voice design.
- Experience defining conversational quality metrics and running LLM evaluations, including LLM-as-a-judge.
- Experience prototyping multimodal experiences across voice, text, visual, and ambient surfaces.
- Familiarity with prompt engineering, model shaping, reinforcement learning, and AI-driven personalization.
- Understanding of WCAG AA standards and accessibility fluency.
- Expertise in working creatively around constraints and navigating ambiguous projects.
- Experience in entertainment, gaming, or streaming media.
- Bachelor's or Master's degree in design, HCI, computer science, linguistics, or equivalent.

title: Duales Studium - Automation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Du möchtest verstehen, wie Roboter, Sensoren und automatisierte Anlagen zusammenspielen?

Bei Amazon setzt du dein Wissen direkt in der Praxis ein. Du arbeitest an Anlagen, die Produkte durch eines der komplexesten Logistiknetzwerke der Welt bewegen. Vom ersten Tag an übernimmst du Verantwortung, arbeitest Seite an Seite mit erfahrenen Automation Engineers und siehst den direkten Einfluss deiner Arbeit.

Als Teil von Amazon eröffnet sich dir ein Universum an Möglichkeiten: Zugang zu modernster Technik, vielfältige Karrierewege und ein Umfeld, in dem deine Ideen zählen und du früh gefördert und gefordert wirst.

Während des dualen Studiums besuchst du die Hochschule, um einen Bachelor of Engineering (B.Eng.) mit Vertiefung Automatisierungstechnik zu erwerben. In einem Trainingszentrum erhältst du eine praktische Grundausbildung, und bei Amazon wendest du dein Wissen direkt an, an der Seite von erfahrenen Automation Engineers, die dich fördern und fordern.

Dabei entwickelst du Kenntnisse in Elektronik und Elektrotechnik, Informationstechnik, Programmierung sowie Automatisierungs- und Steuerungstechnik. Gleichzeitig tauchst du in Zukunftsthemen wie Robotik, Smart Systems und IoT ein.

Beginn: 01.08.2027
Standort: Witten
Hochschule: HS Düsseldorf
Ausbildungszentrum: Siemens AG Düsseldorf

Du tüftelst gerne, packst mit an und willst früh Verantwortung übernehmen? Dann bist du bei uns genau richtig.

Key job responsibilities
• Hardware Engineering und Konfiguration von Anlagen
• Inbetriebnahme komplexer Infrastruktursysteme
• Arbeit mit Automatisierungssystemen und Prozessvisualisierungen
• Intelligente Fabrikautomation mit Cloud-Konnektivität
• IoT-Anwendungen in der Gebäude- und Anlagentechnik
• Installation elektrischer Einrichtungen
• Prüfung von elektrischen, pneumatischen und hydraulischen Steuerungen
• Zusammenarbeit mit erfahrenen Automation Engineers und technischen Teams an realen Projekten

A day in the life
Deine Ausbildung verbindet Theorie und Praxis von Anfang an. Deine theoretische Ausbildung absolvierst du an der Hochschule sowie in einem Trainingszentrum, während du die praktischen Kenntnisse direkt bei Amazon an deinem Standort erwirbst.

Ein typischer Tag? Du analysierst gemeinsam mit erfahrenen Automation Engineers eine Störung an einer Förder- oder Sortieranlage, tauschst Komponenten aus und bringst das System wieder zum Laufen. An einem anderen Tag konfigurierst du eine Steuerung und nimmst neue Technik in Betrieb. Und dann gibt es die Tage, an denen du an einem Projekt rund um Robotik, Sensorik oder IoT mitarbeitest.

Kein Tag ist wie der andere – mal stehst du an der Anlage, mal suchst du Fehler vor Ort, mal analysierst und optimierst du Systeme am Computer.

Du arbeitest von Anfang an mit erfahrenen Automation Engineers zusammen, lernst von ihnen und übernimmst Schritt für Schritt mehr Verantwortung. Du probierst Dinge aus und lernst Fähigkeiten, von denen du vorher nicht wusstest, dass es sie gibt.

title: Senior Systems Engineer, Amazon Special Projects
descriptionHtml:

We focus on creating entirely new products and services with a goal of positively impacting the lives of our customers. No industries or subject areas are out of bounds. We launched products such as Comprehend Medical, Echo Frames and Amazon Explore. If you’re interested in innovating at scale to address big challenges in the world, this is the team for you.
As the Sr. Systems Engineer, you will own the agent daemon that runs on compute nodes, the runtime sandbox that isolates workloads, and the local storage and caching layer that determines which assets are resident and ready to serve. Your work directly determines whether the platform can deliver low-latency ML inference — and whether it can do so reliably at scale.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and implement the agent daemon on Linux, including GPU discovery, availability detection, and sandboxed container execution for ML inference workloads.
- Architect the local caching system — eviction policies, versioned manifests, disk budget management, and efficient update mechanisms that minimize data transfer for large model files.
- Build VRAM management and graceful workload migration logic.
- Integrate hardware attestation with the security engineer and support diverse hardware configurations and fleet onboarding automation.

About the team
Amazon Special Projects is a small, high-autonomy team building new-to-Amazon infrastructure from scratch. The systems component is where software meets hardware: you will build the on-node runtime — the agent, sandbox, GPU manager, and local storage layer — that makes a compute node reliable, secure, and performant. This is systems engineering at its most tangible — your code runs on real hardware and must be resilient to everything the real world throws at it.

Basic qualifications

- 6+ years of programming with at least one modern language such as C++, C#, Java, Python, Golang, PowerShell, Ruby experience
- 6+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 6+ years of designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience leading the design, build and deployment of complex and performant (reliable and scalable) software solutions in production
- 6+ years of systems design, software development, operations, automation, and process improvement experience
- 7+ years of experience in systems programming (Rust, Go, or C++)
- Deep knowledge of Linux internals, including process scheduling, memory management, and storage subsystems
- Hands-on experience with container runtimes (Docker, containers, or custom sandboxes)
- Experience with GPU tooling and management (nvidia-smi, NVML, CUDA runtime)
- Demonstrated ability to build software that runs reliably on heterogeneous hardware

Preferred qualifications

- Knowledge of engineering practices and patterns for the full software/hardware/networks development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, certification, and livesite operations
- Experience taking a leading role in building complex software or computing infrastructure that has been successfully delivered to customers
- Experience designing caching systems with constrained storage budgets (LRU, ARC, or custom policies)
- Background in edge computing, fleet management, or embedded systems engineering
- Familiarity with hardware attestation (TPM, TEE) from the device side
- Experience with storage performance profiling and optimization across hardware types
- Track record of building daemon/agent software that operates unattended for extended periods

title: Business Analyst, Customer Experience, Amazon Air
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Air operates more than 100 flights a day across North America and is growing fast. The Customer Experience (CX) team owns the analytical frameworks that connect fleet performance, network operations, and on-time delivery outcomes for customers.
We are looking for a Business Analyst who can work on complex, ambiguous problems and turn operational data into clear, actionable insights. You will build and maintain the metrics, dashboards, and data pipelines that drive daily and weekly decision-making across the Amazon Air network. Your work will directly shape how the team understands and improves delivery performance for customers.


Key job responsibilities
• Own the design, development, and maintenance of operational dashboards and performance metrics that track delivery quality across the Amazon Air network, including DEA (Delivery Experience Attainment) and related indicators.
• Identify and investigate delivery performance gaps by diving deep into large, complex datasets across multiple data sources including Redshift, Andes, PerfectMile, and DataCentral.
• Build and maintain ETL pipelines and automated reporting solutions that reduce manual effort and improve the speed and accuracy of operational insights.
• Own the Misbucketing AIR process — identifying packages incorrectly attributed to Air operations and driving corrections through data — and continuously improve the intake and classification workflow.
• Support the AirWatch program by maintaining and improving dashboards that provide visibility into aircraft out-of-service events and their downstream impact on delivery performance.
• Partner with supply chain managers and operations leaders to translate business questions into analysis requirements, and present findings to senior stakeholders.
• Recognize and adopt best practices in reporting and analysis: data integrity, test design, analysis validation, and documentation — ensuring pipelines and dashboards can be independently maintained by others.
• Apply generative AI tools to accelerate insight generation and automate routine monitoring and reporting workflows.


A day in the life
On Monday, a delivery performance gap surfaces overnight. You pull the data, trace it to a root cause in the misbucketing pipeline, and have a draft fix to the data engineering team before the morning stand-up.
On Wednesday, an ops leader needs to understand why one gateway is running 15% above its defect target. You build the breakdown, identify the two drivers, and present a one-page summary that gets acted on the same day.
By Friday, you have pushed an updated dashboard to production, cutting a three-hour manual reporting process to fifteen minutes. The team uses it in Monday's business review.
No two weeks look the same.


About the team
Amazon Air's Customer Experience team sets the course for delivering more promises on time across a fast-growing network. We spot risks before they hit customers, and we build the mechanisms that turn a single root cause fix into a lasting improvement across the network.
We work directly with flight planning, linehaul, and data science teams to turn operational insight into action. We use GenAI to automate manual work so we can spend more time solving the next problem instead of reporting on the last one.
We are a small, hands-on team. Every person owns real outcomes, not just analysis.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- 3+ years of tax, finance or a related analytical field experience
- 5+ years of Excel (including VBA, pivot tables, array functions, power pivots, etc.) and data visualization tools such as Tableau experience
- Experience with SQL
- Experience making business recommendations and influencing stakeholders

Preferred qualifications

- Experience partnering with executive-level leaders to identifying and solving business issues
- Experience with SQL and database technologies such as AWS Redshift and expertise in performance tuning and scaling in a DWH environment
- Experience in ETL management/data pipeline
- Experience utilizing R or Python
- Experience in program management, logistics, operations, supply chain, transportation, or a related field
- Experience applying generative AI tools to automate analytical or reporting workflows

title: Area Manager, EF Operations
descriptionHtml:
アマゾンジャパン オペレーションズ部門のEF（External Fulfillment）オペレーションチームでは、チームをリードし、EF拠点のオペレーション管理・改善を行うマネージャーを募集します。
EFチームは、Amazonのお客様が注文した商品の注文処理・配送業務を自社の物流拠点（FC、フルフィルメントセンター）ではなく、メーカー/ 卸売企業の倉庫内や協力会社（以下3PL）の運営する倉庫で行うExternal Fulfillment（外部サイトから顧客への直接出荷）のサービスを拡張することによって、コスト削減、配送スピードの向上、セレクションの拡充、そしてお客様の満足度の向上に貢献しています。
このポジションでは、アマゾンの出荷・在庫能力の一翼を担うEF拠点の運営管理・改善、ピープルマネジメントを通じたメンバー育成が主要な業務になります。マネージャーとして多様なメンバーが能力を発揮できる組織の仕組み作りやカルチャーの醸成を推進いただける方を求めています。

【業務内容】
1．外部委託するオペレーションの標準化を行い、管理指標に基づいた安全な職場環境作り、品質管理、在庫・出荷計画の遂行に責任を持ちます。
2. プロジェクトメンバーとして社内外の取り組みに参加します。案件によっては、プロジェクトオーナーとして広く部門・チーム横断的な取り組みをリードします。
3. マネージャーとしてチームメンバーの育成に責任を持ちます。またチーム全体のDEI文化の醸成に向けた取り組みにも参加して頂きます。

年次、月次、週次で作成されたマスタープランに基づき、達成するべき要件（安全、品質、入荷・出荷の能力、在庫キャパシティ、コスト）毎に個別計画を明確にし、3PL各社のオペレーションが円滑に遂行されることに責任を負います。
また日々のオペレーションを管理するだけでなく、新しいサービスやプログラムの導入、新規拠点の立ち上げなど、3PL各社との調整のみならず、広く社内の他部門（リテールビジネス、セラービジネス、配送オペレーション、ファイナンス、リーガル、人事など）ともコミュニケーションを取り、プロジェクトの立上げから管理運営を行います。

Essential Functions [% of Time]
1.　25%:　EF拠点の管理運営
2.　25%:　指標管理と関係部署との調整
3.　25%:　新規プロジェクト等の取り組み
4.　25%:　チームメンバーの育成・管理

【ポジションの特徴】
・スピード感のある業務
この仕事の最も重要なポイントは、迅速に変化に対応しリードしていく事にあります。EFチームは、３PL各社との協業により、自社の物流拠点（FC）では対応が難しい新しいビジネスや商材にも高い柔軟性をもって取り組み、またスピーディにEF拠点を立ち上げることでAmazonのビジネスの成長戦略を支え、お客様の満足度の向上に貢献しています。
・業務領域の広さ
社内外に広くステークホルダーを持ち、アマゾンのサプライチェーン全体を意識しながら、広い視点を持って業務に取り組める業務領域の広さが特徴です。

【働き方について】
勤務時間は、原則、9：00～18：00で、月1-2日土日勤務あり(代休取得)
プロジェクト対応や現場確認など業務上の必要性から出張もありますが、メリハリをつけて業務に取り組める環境です。

title: Sr. Risk Manager, Brand Protection Policy and Governance
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's Worldwide Brand Protection organization ensures that brands can protect their Intellectual Property, and customers can shop with confidence across Amazon's global stores. We do this through ML-powered detection systems that identify abusive actors at enrollment, identity verification pipelines that gate access to brand privileges, and automated enforcement mechanisms that detect catalog manipulation and coordinated abuse at scale.

We are seeking a motivated, data-driven Sr. Risk Manager to join the Brand Protection Policy & Governance team, which owns the development, evolution, and consistent application of Brand Protection's policy frameworks across Amazon's global stores. As the threat landscape shifts, this team creates and adapts policies that define enforcement actions, shape operational processes, and govern seller-facing communications. This role bridges investigative execution with strategic coordination — performing deep dive investigations, coordinating across technical, program, and operational teams, and owning organizational playbooks that enable consistent, scalable investigation execution across cross-functional teams.

The ideal candidate is self-driven, takes initiative, and thrives in ambiguity — independently identifying opportunities, shaping direction, and moving work forward when the path isn't clear. They think both tactically and strategically, equally effective resolving a complex investigation as they are influencing cross-organizational priorities, streamlining processes, and removing barriers that slow teams down. They bring strong business judgment, analytical rigor, and excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a proven track record of succeeding in a customer-driven workplace under tight deadlines. They possess the ability to assess risk, identify and propose multiple solutions, and weigh strategic trade-offs to arrive at the right call in complex, ambiguous situations. They communicate with clarity and conviction to senior leaders and earn trust through consistent, high-quality delivery.


Key job responsibilities
- Serve as the primary point of contact for Brand Protection escalations — leading deep-dive investigations, driving end-to-end resolution across cross-functional stakeholders within SLA commitments, synthesizing findings into clear communications, and ensuring systematic delivery of risk mitigation outcomes
- Own ad hoc initiatives and cross-functional projects to address emerging risks and operational gaps
- Design and optimize workflows across case resolution, reporting, and process improvement while balancing competing priorities and navigating ambiguity
- Partner with internal legal teams and policy owners as needed to interpret laws, regulations, and business policies
- Define risk strategy and manage the full lifecycle of cross-functional risk programs — driving measurable risk reduction and facilitating alignment across Operations, Product, Engineering, Science, Legal, and other stakeholder teams
- Shape long-term perspective for risk-related business and technology decisions, partnering with stakeholders to prioritize risk mitigation projects
- Develop playbooks and frameworks for risk mitigation and incident response that standardize investigation approaches, enable scalable execution, and drive measurable outcomes across cross-functional teams
- Write clear and compelling narratives and present effectively to directors and VPs

Basic qualifications

- 6+ years of compliance, audit or risk management experience

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent

Preferred qualifications

- Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent certification
- Experience leveraging technology and implementing lean principles / Six Sigma methodologies to drive process improvements or equivalent
- Master's degree or equivalent

title: System Development Engineer, Amazon Leo, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations with or without reliable connectivity. Our Payload Integration and Testing (PIT) team validates the end-to-end network interface communication system both on the ground prior to launch and in-orbit to ensure we are providing customers a best-in-class experience. We're the final software quality gate, ensuring what customers experience on-orbit matches our design intent.

As a System Development Engineer, you'll design and build the test automation framework and procedures that validate our satellite network end to end -- and the full stack it runs on, from the device-interface layer that drives physical hardware up through the infrastructure and operational tooling that keep our hardware-in-the-loop (HILT) test venues running reliably at scale. You'll write the automation frameworks and test harnesses that exercise the system, the low-level interface code and device drivers that let those harnesses command and read back from lab hardware over protocols like serial/UART, I2C/SPI, USB, Ethernet, and instrument-control interfaces, and the compute, networking, provisioning, and observability underneath that keep it all healthy. The technical scope is broad and systems-oriented: you'll build test-orchestration and automation software, architect and automate cloud and on-premise infrastructure, integrate and bring up lab hardware down to the register and command level, and drive the operational excellence practices that keep a high-stakes, 24/7 test environment reliable. If you love building test automation, enjoy working at the intersection of software, networking, and physical hardware, and want to solve unique operational challenges in the space domain, this is an exceptional opportunity.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, and maintain test automation frameworks, test harnesses, and orchestration software that validate the satellite network end to end

- Develop automated test suites and the tooling engineers use to author, run, schedule, and debug tests across distributed HITL venues

- Write and maintain the low-level interface code and device drivers that let test systems command and read back from lab hardware over protocols such as serial/UART, I2C/SPI, USB, Ethernet, and instrument-control interfaces (e.g., SCPI)

- Perform device bring-up and integration: understand hardware command sets and register maps, debug at the protocol level, and build the abstraction layers that expose hardware to higher-level test automation

- Design, build, and operate the infrastructure and networking that connects distributed hardware-in-the-loop test venues to cloud services

- Automate provisioning, configuration, and deployment of test environments using infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD pipelines

- Build and own monitoring, alarming, dashboards, and observability for test orchestration systems and the infrastructure they depend on

- Drive operational excellence: on-call response, incident management, root-cause analysis, and systemic fixes that prevent recurrence

- Identify and resolve systemic reliability, scaling, and performance issues across the test stack -- automation, compute, network, and storage

- Collaborate with software engineers, applied scientists, systems engineers, and test teams to translate test and operational requirements into robust automation and infrastructure

- Write clean, maintainable, well-documented software following engineering best practices, and participate in design and code reviews

title: Sr. Financial Analyst
descriptionHtml:
Senior Financial Analyst, FAIM Finance (Amazon Ads)

Amazon Ads is building toward a future where an advertiser specifies a few marketing parameters (budget, success definition, which products to promote) and a set of AI agents handles the rest. The Full Funnel Agentic Intelligence and Models (FAIM) organization owns that bet: the Ads Nova agent, the Ads Nova model it reasons with, and the full-funnel campaign products that put them in front of advertisers. FAIM Finance is the team that answers whether the bet is paying off, and at what cost.

We are hiring a Senior Financial Analyst to own financial planning and analysis for this organization: the operating plan, the monthly actuals and forecast, the business reviews, and the models that translate agent and model usage into revenue and cost. This is a ground-up build. The products are new, the cost structure is GPU and compute heavy with inference costs that scale with every advertiser conversation, and the forecasting methods have to be invented rather than inherited. You will work alongside a small team of finance managers, business intelligence engineers, and data engineers, with regular exposure to the leaders who run FAIM and to senior leadership across Ads Finance. If you want a finance seat where the P&L looks nothing like a traditional advertising business and the decisions are still being made, keep reading.

What you'll own

- The FAIM operating plan and forecast: annual planning (OP1/OP2), quarterly forecasts, and monthly actuals with variance analysis across revenue, headcount, and infrastructure spend
- The business review mechanism: weekly, monthly, and quarterly reviews that leaders trust for accuracy and read for the story behind the number
- Driver-based models that connect product usage (advertisers, campaigns, agent conversations, tokens, GPU hours) to revenue and cost to serve, for products with little or no history to extrapolate from
- The investment cases: financial support for compute and GPU requests, headcount asks, and new product bets, including the analysis in documents that go to senior leadership

Key job responsibilities

- Drive the planning cycle: build and maintain the FAIM financial model, consolidate inputs from Product, Engineering, and Science, and own the bridge between plan, forecast, and actuals
- Run the monthly close analysis: explain variances, identify root causes, state the financial implication, and follow through on the actions that come out of it
- Partner with product and engineering leaders to anticipate business needs, interpret trends, and evaluate the economics of new products, pricing, and infrastructure decisions
- Build the models behind investment decisions (compute capacity, headcount, pricing) and write the financial sections of documents that senior leaders act on
- Coordinate the business review mechanisms, ensuring reporting accuracy and clear communication of results and recommendations
- Work with the team's business intelligence and data engineers so the finance data platform answers the questions the P&L raises; define what the business needs to measure and how it is read
- Lead projects to automate, simplify, or scale finance processes, including AI-enabled tools that reduce manual work and defects
- Uphold strong financial controllership: accurate accruals, clean cost allocation, and documented SOPs that let others pick up the work

We're looking for an analyst who brings

- 3+ years of finance, FP&A, or related analytical experience, and a bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics, business, or a related field
- Strong financial modeling skills: driver-based forecasts, scenario analysis, and the attention to detail to make the numbers tie
- Experience building financial and operational reports that inform decisions, and applying key performance indicators to explain what happened and why
- Working SQL and advanced Excel fluency, with the habit of pulling your own data rather than waiting for it
- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain a variance or a recommendation to a senior leader in plain language
- Experience in advertising, software, or cloud infrastructure finance, especially with usage-based cost structures (compute, GPU, inference), is a plus
- Python or equivalent for analysis and automation, and familiarity with QuickSight or similar reporting tools
- Experience supporting a new product or 0-to-1 business where forecasting is built from drivers rather than trends
- AI-native working style: using tools such as Kiro, Claude Code, or equivalent to automate recurring analysis and catch defects faster
- Comfort operating in ambiguity, with a bias for action and the judgment to know when precision matters and when direction is enough

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of finance, accounting, or related analytical field experience
- Bachelor's degree in business, finance, accounting, tax, economics, or a related analytical field

Preferred qualifications

- 4+ years of participating in continuous improvement projects in your team to scale and improve controllership with measurable results experience
- MBA, or CPA
- Knowledge of Tableau
- Experience working with large-scale data mining and reporting tools (examples: SQL, MS Access, Essbase, Cognos) and other financial systems (examples: Oracle, SAP, Lawson, JD Edwards)

At Amazon, your career doesn’t follow a straight line. It accelerates, twists, and challenges you in ways you never expected.
